Ballard has got a little bit of Konsa’s shirt too and there’s a bit of tugging but that in itself, with all the bits and bobs going on, doesn’t jump out as a clear and obvious error, so they stay with the on-field decision. What is important to note is the light touch from VARs this season.

Lots of people will say penalty. Others will say not for me. Attwell was right to say check complete, confirming the penalty. If a penalty hadn’t been awarded, however, there would have been no intervention either because it’s not a clear and obvious error. It’s what we would term a check complete either way.

Chris Foy is a former Premier League referee

Sports.title: De Zerbi backs ‘sensitive guy’ Solanke to find form before tricky Anfield trip
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has no doubt Dominic Solanke will rediscover his best levels as the head coach made clear he had left no stone unturned in the mission to solve Tottenham’s goalscoring problem.

Spurs go to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday after the 0-0 home draw with Everton in the Premier League on Saturday; they have not found the net in their four matches in the competition. Tottenham did beat Charlton 5-1 at home in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Solanke is the only forward in De Zerbi’s squad to have enjoyed a prolific season in England’s top division; he scored 19 times for Bournemouth in 2023-24, which convinced Tottenham to pay £55m for him. The 29-year-old has 22 additional goals in the Premier League, 12 of them for Spurs. De Zerbi has Omar Marmoush, who scored seven times in the league for Manchester City in the second half of 2024-25 after joining from Eintracht Frankfurt in January. That apart, the pickings for De Zerbi’s attacking players have been slim in the competition.

Solanke, whose pre-season was undermined by an injury sustained on the club’s tour of New Zealand and Australia, was ineffective against Everton and a target for criticism is some quarters. De Zerbi will keep the faith. He remembers being amazed at how well Solanke played for Bournemouth against his Brighton team in September 2023. Brighton won 3-1 but Solanke scored. De Zerbi knows that when Solanke is fully fit the goals and performances will follow. He intends to involve the former Liverpool striker at Anfield, whether from the start or as a substitute.

“Dom is a sensitive guy,” De Zerbi said. “He needs to feel full confidence – and from myself, he has big, big confidence. I believe he can score 10-15 goals, for sure. He’s already scored in Bournemouth so why not he can score in Tottenham? It’s the same sport.

“[He is] sensitive because he’s a smart guy. Sensitive guys are smart. Maybe [he has had] many injuries, maybe he doesn’t feel in the best physical condition, maybe he would like to do something different on the pitch. But now he’s not fit yet. He has to play. It can be important for him [at Anfield]. And then I think he comes back to the player who was in Bournemouth. I remember Brighton v Bournemouth in the Amex Stadium; he was incredible. I said to my assistant: ‘Who is this striker?’”

View image in fullscreen Dominic Solanke scores Tottenham’s second goal in their 5-1 Carabao Cup second round victory over Charlton. Photograph: John Walton/PA

De Zerbi continues to try to bond his players away from the pitch. He said he had again taken them for dinner in Mayfair last week and paid the bill. “As long as I keep some money for my cigarettes, then no problem,” he said with a smile.

De Zerbi is leaning heavily into video analysis, going through clips from matches in team meetings and giving the players individual ones to study. There has been an emphasis in training on attacking crosses in the right way and regaining possession in the final third. The players have also stayed behind for extra shooting practice of their own volition, De Zerbi said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If we want to change from the last two or three seasons we have to be stronger here,” he said, pointing to his head. “We have to believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. Or we change. You can change players or change coaches … change, change, change and nothing changes. Or you stay with the head, stay humble and with the right spirit to work. I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.”

De Zerbi reported that Sandro Tonali would miss the Liverpool game with a knock, and Richarlison will not be involved despite being eligible for the Carabao Cup; the Brazilian forward was omitted from Spurs’ Premier League squad.

Pedro Porro is still out but Destiny Udogie is back, and Mohammed Kudus is ready to start. James Maddison, though, is still unavailable. De Zerbi will make changes and he mentioned Marcos Senesi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Ben Davies, Lucas Bergvall and Mathys Tel as being in contention to come into the XI. Spurs have not won at Anfield in 17 matches.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola tells Liverpool forwards they must do more to make his system work
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has shifted the focus on to Liverpool’s forwards for the team’s uninspiring display against Fulham, insisting they need to give more to make his system work.

The head coach admitted his team took “a step backwards” with their goalless draw on Saturday. His central midfield pairing of Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai struggled to contain their Fulham counterparts, winning two of five duels and one of nine duels respectively. But Iraola believes the problems started further forward with the pressing of Liverpool’s expensively assembled attack.

“It’s not a matter of just the midfielders,” he said. “When we have been good collectively the mid­fielders have looked a lot better and recovered more balls. It’s not because they are winning duels that they play better, it’s because we are helping them more to win the duels.

“If the ones up front do their job very well then the defenders and midfielders look good. If we are allowing them to defend one v one all the time and we are not aggressive, then our defenders will also struggle. If the players ahead of you are doing their job then you look a better midfielder or defender because you win more easier duels, you have more chance of winning one. It is more collective.

“It isn’t about changing this player for that player. That’s the help we have to give to our defenders and midfielders so everyone looks better, looks smarter and are in better positions.”

Iraola is unlikely to field the same frontline of Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Víctor Muñoz when Tottenham visit Anfield in the Carabao Cup third round on Tuesday. Trey Nyoni is pressing for a start in midfield and Iraola confirmed that Giorgi Mamardashvili, whom he tried to sign for Bournemouth, would replace ­Alisson in goal.

View image in fullscreen The Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili will make his first appearance of the season in the Carabao Cup tie against Tottenham. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images

On the issues of Saturday, which contributed to a third draw in four Premier League games, he also said: “Compared to previous games, we won the ball a lot lower in the pitch. We don’t concede a lot, and the only big chance we conceded was our goal‑kick that we messed up. But we were recovering the ball always very low and when that happens you have to attack against 11 players and that makes it more difficult to make the difference.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In previous games we could win it a lot higher and use our quick transitions to attack against less players and use the space better. That is key to our system. We need to recover the ball as high as possible because it makes the offensive side a lot easier, and we have more situations to attack in one v one.”

Sports.title: ‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisis | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
Kiat Lim wanted to see Valencia play so badly, so that is what he did. It was week four in La Liga, 6 September, and for the first time since he was given the presidency 18 months earlier, the owner’s 33-year-old son was going to watch his team play a competitive game. He was going to do it from the inside, too, so he took a flight to Spain, landing at Manises in a black mask and cap, a van to the hotel, then the team bus to Mestalla. He looked through the window as they rolled along Avenida Suecia, a huge, noisy crowd waiting, but when he got off and headed through the iron gate with its ornate club badge, he saw that this was no welcome.

Above him as he went in were giant portraits of Mario Kempes, Antonio Puchades, Juan Sol, Gaizka Mendieta, David Villa and Santiago Cañizares, footballers from a better time; around him were yellow banners and whistles for the footballers there now. Inside, Lim saw the game start with the lower south stand empty as fans stayed away until the 19th minute, the sound of another protest drifting in from the street. They were out there still when, sitting alongside Joan Laporta, he saw Lamine Yamal score the sixth-minute opener then get a second. And although that, also from Lamine Yamal, was ruled out, he eventually saw Barcelona get four more, presiding over a 5-0 debut defeat.

He had seen supporters leave early, seen those that stayed turn towards him, chanting for him and his family to leave for good. He had seen the hankies come out and his players head into the tunnel heads bowed. He heard his manager insist that they were hurt but not sunk. What he did not see – what no one had seen yet but everyone would see soon enough – was the verdict from the bench.

Withdrawn after an hour to a standing ovation, the World Cup winner Rodri took a towel and turned to Pau Cubarsí. “This lot are very weak, eh?” Spain’s captain said. “Very weak, mate. Very bad.” He asked where they finished last season, pulled a face that said seriously?! when he was told just outside Europe, and noted that they had not left their own half. Valencia, he said, were malísimo. Awful.

View image in fullscreen Rodri was caught on camera calling his former club ‘very weak’. Photograph: David Ramos/Getty Images

The sequence was caught on camera by El Día Después, and soon it was everywhere. Rodri called Valencia’s captain José Luis Gayà, saying sorry. After Barcelona’s Champions League win against Feyenoord three days later, he offered a public apology. It was, the Valencia coach, Carlos Corberán, said, a touch of self-preservation about his reaction, the least Rodri could do: apology accepted but his “unfortunate” words had “not been born of respect”. Yet there was no taunt, no mocking, no derision, no sign of a smile; instead there was a kind of shocked sadness. His words had not been thrown in anyone’s faces and were not for sharing. They were also true.

And if Corberán noted that “Mestalla had applauded him too”, an aggravating factor, some of them would do it again: it had needed saying. Within a few days someone had designed T-shirts declaring: “They’re very bad.” Underneath it read: “We’re all Rodri.” They had barely started printing off before Corberán was gone. Shoot the manager, not the messenger.

Barcelona’s victory over Valencia last Sunday was the third time in four games that they had scored five. Three days later they did it again. But those were not really the same – at Mestalla it was hard to avoid the feeling that Hansi Flick’s side could have scored 10 if they wanted to – and this was not just about Barcelona, this was about them. Valencia really are malísimo. Four games into season, they had conceded nine and scored one – and that was a gift, scored by a man who is now seriously injured. They had a solitary point, were bottom, and things were not about to get any better. This Friday, they lost the Used To Be Big Derby, 1-0 to Sevilla at the Sanchez Pizjuan, Juan Iglesias’s header condemning Valencia to the worst start in their history and Corberán to the sack.

There is something about these two; the last two times Sevilla fired their manager (García Pimienta and Matías Almeyda), it was after defeat to Valencia, while this is the third time Valencia fired a coach having lost at the Sánchez-Pizjuán: Quique Sánchez Flores in 2007, Nuno Espírito Santo in 2015 and now Corberán. Sánchez Flores got sacked at 4am. This time the wait was a little longer, if not much. When Valencia’s players and staff got back to Paterna to collect their cars in the small hours of Saturday, 100 fans waited to shout abuse and by the time training had finished there on Sunday morning the decision was made. Corberán was told during a video call from Singapore, Lim 10,000km away again.

The coach who arrived in December 2024 with Valencia in the relegation zone and pulled them up to 12th; the manager who saw them slip into the relegation zone again at the halfway stage last season only to pull clear all the way to the edge of Europe, would not get the chance to try again. Just five weeks into the season, two months after his contract was extended for another year, and 10 days after the CEO, Ron Gourlay, insisted that stability meant standing by a coach he believed in even if fans, some players and an increasingly belligerent media might not, he was gone.

Mind you, Gourlay has gone too. At that defiant two-hour, via-translator press conference Gourlay insisted that if his critics were going to wait for him to go, their coffee would get cold, but he has been sacked along with all his staff. Braulio Vázquez, has joined from Osasuna – even though Braulio recently said Osasuna are the “only real club left” – given the task of finding a new coach, with the B team manager taking over for the time being. His arrival ushers in a restructuring and a “new era” at Valencia, the statement said.

Braulio knows the club – he was sporting director there between 2011 and 2013 and his son is the left-back – and has been successful at Osasuna, widely considered a more convincing candidate than the man who was there until Sunday afternoon. Few fans are sorry to see Corberán go: in fact they have been chanting for just that, the social fracture another factor. A change of coach can change things, a change of CEO or sporting director too. Look at Valencia’s squad and they should and probably will be better than this, the academy keeps producing talent, and Mestalla still fills weekly. There are coaches out there that would convince, with Ernesto Valverde and Jagoba Arrasate’s names the first to be floated. They certainly couldn’t be much worse than they have been so far. But patience is thin and faith thinner, a pessimism long since having crept in, and not unjustifiably so.

The only thing most fans want of the owners now is for them to leave which plays a part too, everyone caught in the never-ending tension. It is less than two years since Gourley took over, a year since Lim said that they have a “proper sporting plan now ... which is not to say we did not in the past but now we have professionals in place.” He was already the sixth man to supposedly have responsibility for signings since Peter Lim bought the club in 2014. Óscar Sánchez will be Valencia’s fifteenth coach since then – and even Voro, the eternal caretaker who has had the job six times does not want it any more. Only Nuno and Marcelino have better win percentages than Corberán. This summer, they spent €9m (£7.7m); 13 clubs spent more. More than 20 players have come in and gone out in the last two years. Over the last seven seasons they have spent short of €70m; they have sold for more than €230m.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Corberán was sacked by Valencia after their worst start to a season in their history. Photograph: Fran Santiago/Getty Images

There was a line in Rodri’s apology that talked about context and context is everything: Valencia being bad was not one Sunday; the fear is that it’s any given Sunday, that the days when they were good may be gone. He said that his comments were born of surprise, sadness, but the saddest thing is many weren’t surprised at all. This is what it is, they thought, grateful that someone else said it; forgive them if they do not foresee a way out. Yet if ambition must be adjusted it is hard not to hold on to what you were, your identity still, and maybe that’s a problem too. The Valencia Rodri returned to is not the Valencia he left behind. The year he went to England, they were a Champions League team; they have not made Europe since. And on Sunday he was right, Corberán taking the fall within a week.

“We all want Valencia to get back to where they should be, one of the best clubs in our league,” Rodri said three days later, but he had already said enough, a truth told. Sitting in the stands, Lim had just about seen enough too.

Sports.title: European football: Inter roar back to beat Udinese and join Roma at the top
Sports.content:
Inter fought back ⁠from two goals down ​to beat Udinese 5-3 on Monday, maintaining their perfect Serie A start alongside Roma, who won 2-0 at Torino before Saturday’s match between ⁠the joint leaders. Both sides have 12 points from four matches and share top spot before their encounter at the Stadio Olimpico, while Como are third on 10 points ⁠after beating Parma 2-1.

Udinese stunned Inter with two goals in the opening 16 minutes, as James Abankwah headed home ​unmarked after nine minutes before Jurgen Ekkelenkamp doubled ‌the visitors’ lead with a ‌close-range finish seven minutes later. Inter hit back through Carlos Augusto, whose long-range effort flew into the bottom corner, ‌before Nicolò Barella levelled 10 minutes before half-time.

The champions completed the turnaround in the 59th minute when Marcus Thuram netted from inside the box after Andy Diouf’s cutback from the byline. Francesco Esposito added a fourth and Ange-Yoan Bonny made it 5-2 with 11 minutes remaining. Udinese pulled one back in stoppage time through Idrissa Gueye, but it proved no more than a consolation.

There was an injury concern for Inter as John Stones limped off with an apparent hamstring injury just after the hour mark. The England centre-back was making his first start after joining on a free transfer this summer.

The Inter manager, Cristian Chivu, confirmed Stones would have to be fully assessed to determine the extent of the issue. “I don’t know, I haven’t had a chance to talk to him,” Chivu told Dazn. “I think he felt something on his flexor [muscle], and he will probably need to get some tests done.”

View image in fullscreen Roma scorers Niccolò Pisilli and Donyell Malen celebrate at the final whistle. Photograph: Alessandro Di Marco/EPA

Roma made it four ‌wins from four thanks to goals from Donyell Malen and Niccolò Pisilli at Torino. Malen broke the deadlock five minutes before the interval after ​pouncing on a misplaced pass from goalkeeper Lucas Perri that had been intercepted by Paulo Dybala. Pisilli wrapped up the win in stoppage time, firing home from an angle after Gianluca Mancini kept the ball in play near the byline.

The Roma coach, Gian Piero Gasperini ,praised the understanding between Malen and Dybala. “Clearly, these are two players who are very talented ⁠individually, but they also complete each other as a pair. They combine beautifully ​to create goals in many games,” ​he told Dazn Italia.

Como followed up their winning Champions League debut against RB Leipzig with a 2-1 home win over Parma, with Jacobo Ramón and Kaiki Bruno scoring for Cesc Fàbregas’s side. “This is an important victory for me as a coach, because I am starting to realise what team we could become,” Fàbregas said.

View image in fullscreen Natan (centre) and his Real Betis teammates fought back from 1-0 down to beat Villarreal 2-1. Photograph: José Jordan/AFP/Getty Images

Meanwhile in Spain, Real Betis secured a 2-1 win at Villarreal to move third in La Liga and leave their opponents in the relegation zone. Goals from Cucho Hernández and Natan helped Betis claim three points and pull level with Real Madrid, after Gerard Moreno opened the scoring for the home side.

“Right now everything’s going against us, teams are punishing us,” Moreno told Movistar. “We have to stick together and demand more of ourselves … maybe when we go behind, anxiety kicks in and it’s more difficult. It’s hard to explain [how few] points we have... we have to be a team now more than ever.”

Sports.title: PSG have finally won a game in Ligue 1 – but they were far from convincing
Sports.content:
It was just a flicker. Ferran Torres picks the ball up and passes it to João Neves. The Portugal midfielder plays it into Ousmane Dembélé, who has lured in Raphaël Le Guen and eliminates him with a mesmeric first-time back-heel into the path of Torres.

The Brest defence are just cones in a training drill, mere extras in this work of art as the Spaniard glides back into the scene to pass the ball into Egil Selvik’s bottom-left corner from 25 yards; it happened in slow motion, but was too quick for the Norwegian goalkeeper to react.

It is a move that had the slick and elegant fluidity of what we have come to expect from Paris Saint-Germain. Just four minutes in, the champions were ahead and the Stade Francis Le-Blé anticipated a show of force, a statement from their visitors.

Luis Enrique had described PSG’s start to the Ligue 1 season as catastrophic. A comfortable 6-1 win against Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League last Wednesday signalled a welcome return to form. The Sopposition manager, none other than Yaya Touré, described his opponents on the night as a machine – we have heard that before.

But once again, PSG were defective in Brittany on Sunday night, even if they did leave with all three points. Torres’s sublime finish was the only goal of the game. It was the Spaniard’s sixth since joining from Barcelona in the summer. All of his six efforts on target this season have found the net. He is clearly still riding the crest of a wave of confidence, having scored the winner in the World Cup final.

Torres’s supreme confidence is not shared by his teammates. Vitinha in particular has yet to resurface since the summer break and PSG are suffering from the lack of incision he usually provides. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is not quite back to his usual levels either and going into this game, there were creeping doubts about Matvey Safonov in goal. The Russian was at fault last weekend when Stanis Idumbo finished at his near post to secure a win for Monaco. It was at his near post he conceded to Kai Havertz in the Champions League final in May; if there is a weakness in PSG, Safonov was the most likely candidate.

But it is only thanks to him that PSG ended a run of five games without a win against French opponents. He was not forced into action when Nuno Mendes played Kamory Doumbia in one-on-one in the second half, the Mali international striking the outside of the PSG post.

Safonov did get a strong hand down low to his left when Doumbia rose highest to thunder a header towards goal and in the dying stages Pathé Mboup’s curled effort to the far post was tipped around the corner.

View image in fullscreen Goalkeeper Matvey Safonov kept PSG in the game with a number of saves. Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty Images

Brest finished with a higher xG than the European champions, but had no points to show for it. Moments of brilliance in both areas were the difference. But that is what PSG are confined to at the minute: moments, flickers of brilliance.

“It was the worst of our four Ligue 1 matches, even if we won,” said Luis Enrique. “In the other three matches, we showed a high level at the back, but our opponents scored every chance. This time, it was the opposite.”

Alarm bells are not ringing. PSG often start slowly and it is only the quality of opposition faced at the start of the last campaign that ensured there was not such a significant deficit to the leaders. They are five points behind Lille, Monaco and Rennes, all of whom are on 10 points.

Last week, Marquinhos said that it was “a matter of ambition and motivation” as PSG hoped to replicate the success of the past two seasons. Just like Torres’s passed finish, PSG are all about timing and they have a knack for peaking at the right moment.

There were no doubts Brest were up to the occasion. The Stade Francis Le-Blé was a cauldron of emotion as Eric Roy was commemorated. The Brest manager, who guided the club into European competition for the first time, in 2024, died in June due to pancreatic cancer that began when he was appointed as the club’s manager in January 2023. His diagnosis was never made public.

Roy’s daughter, Victoria-Rose, spoke on the pitch before the match, “King Eric” shirts were worn on the sidelines and there were further moments of commemoration in the stands throughout the game. Hugo Magnetti said they had played for Roy. “He would have been proud of us, but he would have also ticked us off for missing some big chances.”

The game, at times, felt like a subplot, but what happened in it was not inconsequential. Some of those fears about waning “ambition and motivation” were deepened, as was a crisis of confidence among some of PSG’s key players, despite victory. But there were also flickers of brilliance Luis Enrique must hope will become more enduring as the season progresses.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Lille 2-0 Troyes Le Mans 2-2 Lens Brest 0-1 PSG Strasbourg 1-1 Monaco Auxerre 1-0 Nice Le Havre 0-0 Angers Lorient 2-2 Toulouse Paris FC 0-0 Lyon Rennes 1-0 Marseille Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

Will Still and Auxerre have their first points on the board thanks to their young English forward Cameron Archer. The Southampton loanee made his debut last weekend and scored a stunner in a 3-1 defeat to Lyon. This weekend he scored the only goal of the game against Nice. The win drags Auxerre off the bottom of the table – a place now occupied by their opponents on the day. Nice, without a win, have scored once in their first four matches. Their coach, Olivier Pantaloni, says there are traces of last season’s difficult campaign lingering in the minds of his players. They must quickly dispel them in order to avoid a repeat.

Four games in and the temperature is already rising in Marseille. The season started well, with a 4-0 home win to Strasbourg on opening day, but they have since lost to Monaco, Paris FC and Rennes. There is no real shame in any of those defeats; the matches were close and the opponents are expected to be in the race for Europe. “We can rival these teams but not yet beat them,” said Bruno Génésio after the 1-0 defeat at Rennes on Friday. Génésio added it was not up to him to state the club’s objectives this season – a clear message to his superiors. “We may need to explain things more clearly Maybe we have to say it so that people can understand.” The lack of quality and depth in the squad says enough; Marseille are outsiders in the race for European football.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Leeds sniffed vulnerability and went for the kill in 4-1 horror show for Newcastle, writes CRAIG HOPE - this was a warning over where their season could end up, while Whites eye race for Europe
Sports.content:
Identical records coming into this, poles and goals apart coming out. Leeds bullied and bettered Newcastle and are deservedly up to third in the Premier League. Their unbeaten start is genuine and so are the prospects of them challenging for European football this season, nearly a quarter of a century after their last continental campaign. Newcastle’s start always felt less real, and so it proved on a night when Daniel Farke’s side were as brilliant and boisterous as those in the stands. Elland Road was a bear pit and, from the off, it was clear that their visitors were in for a mauling. To think, they’re in the process of making this place even bigger and more intimidating. Those words capture Dominic Calvert-Lewin, too. He should be in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad this week after a centre-forward showing that was as powerful as it was precise. He deserved two goals - the dubious awards panel gave his first to a strand of Jayden Bogle’s hair - but there is no such committee to rob him of the man-of-the-match prize. ‘It was a top-class performance during the whole game,’ said Farke. ‘But we can’t get cocky or too big-time. This should give us huge confidence going forward. ‘As for Dominic, he is one of the best strikers in the league in this form.’ This 3-0 Leeds defeat marked the night the result caught up with their performances Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the star of the show as he continued his fine form at Elland Road For Newcastle, this was a night when the result finally caught up with performance. Unbeaten in three at the outset of the Premier League and lauded for their summer business, autumn and winter might not be so cheery on the evidence of this horror show. Matthias Jaissle’s side were three down by half-time, and it was no surprise at all. Be that on the basis of what played out here or, more so, performances of the past 10 days. An unconvincing 1-0 win at Millwall in the Carabao Cup came on the back of an equally sketchy 2-2 draw at home to Bournemouth. This, then, was in the post, and Calvert-Lewin was the home side’s delivery man. He was not the only one to profit from opposition weak in the tackle, wayward in the pass and woefully short of ideas in attack. Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu bossed a midfield that was superior by every metric. At times, you wondered if the hosts had an extra man. You wondered more how Newcastle have won such praise for their character and resilience in recent weeks. There were none of those traits on show this time. Jaissle said: ‘Not only one thing went wrong. We couldn’t bring the fundamentals in the first half. We couldn’t match the intensity of Leeds, in duals or physicality. That should be the basics of football. Unforced errors were taking place. We needed to find the right reaction on the pitch, and we struggled with that.’ Newcastle’s numbers have not felt sustainable. They had conceded a league-high 45 shots over the first three games and, at the other end, their cumulative XG was just over one per 90 minutes. This will infuriate traditionalists - those who cherish the scoreline - but an expected league position had Newcastle 19th going into this weekend. A lot, it seemed, rested on the slender shoulders on Matias Fernandez-Pardo in reversing the numbers. The 21-year-old, a £51million marquee arrival from Lille this month, was making his full debut. ‘Eden Hazard without the end product’ was how one Belgian journalist described the forward on the day he signed, much to the irritation of black-and-white ears listening on local radio. So, was there any merit in the unflattering assessment? MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Leeds (3-4-2-1): Trafford 6; Justin 7, Elvedi 6, Muharemovic 6; Bogle 7, Ampadu 8, Tanaka 8 (Aaronson 72, 6), Gudmundsson 7 (Bard 72, 6); Stach 6, Okafor 7 (Wilson 72, 6); Calvert-Lewin 9 Subs: Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha Manager: Daniel Farke 8 Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 57), Thiaw 5, Botman 3, Hall 5; Miley 4 (Bamba 80), Gonzalez 5 (Steur 19, 4); Murphy 4 (Toure 57, 6), Wissa 5, Barnes 4; Fernandez-Pardo 4 (Willock 57, 4) Subs: Pope, Livramento, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley Manager: Matthias Jaissle 4 Ref: M Salisbury 7 After 25 minutes, the hot-takes felt cold, given Fernandez-Pardo had touched the ball only four times, and one of those was an accidental handball inside his own area. By the time he made way in the 57th minute, the touch count had reached 15, but none of them memorable. What Fernandez-Pardo learnt here is that speed of foot counts for nothing when faced with speed of thought. ‘We had to bury the game after a good start and that is what we did,’ said Farke. Leeds’ third goal on the stroke of half-time was the one that sealed the zip on Newcastle’s body bag. That goal was about Calvert-Lewin’s force and Newcastle’s complete lack of it, the striker barging his way through Sven Botman before finishing from six yards. The opener, 13 minutes earlier, was officially a Lewis Miley own goal, but it owed everything to Ao Tanaka, who started the move amid space in midfield and finished it amid space in midfield. It was his 20-yard shot that deflected in off the Newcastle youngster, who like many of his team-mates endured a torrid night. His midfield sidekick, Sean Steur, was guilty of the stray pass that set Leeds on their way to a second, when Calvert-Lewin headed in from a James Justin cross, only for replays to reveal the ball clipping the head of Bogle. Marquee signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo struggled, but that says more about the failings behind him Technical weaknesses were always likely to catch up with the Magpies this season The fourth, in the 59th minute, was a smart Noah Okafor finish after he reacted quickest to a loose ball from a long throw-in. But Leeds had been quicker to first, second and third balls all night. The home fans were chanting for five when Baz Toure nicked an 89th-minute consolation. The away end had long since lost their voice and their solemn mood reflected a team who had made precious little noise on the pitch. This was a brutal reality check and serves as a warning for where their season could be headed. Leeds, meanwhile, are looking up - at Arsenal and Manchester City.

Sports.title: Tom Aspinall announces he is vacating UFC heavyweight title after 'multiple surgeries, accidents and infections' as British fighter admits he's 'absolutely gutted' in emotional social media post
Sports.content:
Tom Aspinall announces he is vacating UFC heavyweight title after 'multiple surgeries, accidents and infections' as British fighter admits he's 'absolutely gutted' in emotional social media post

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tom Aspinall has vacated his UFC heavyweight title due to 'ongoing complications' with eye injuries.

The Englishman last fought in October last year, when his title defence against Ciryl Gane ended as a no-contest after multiple eye pokes.

Aspinall was subsequently diagnosed with a rare condition called Brown's syndrome in both eyes and has had multiple surgeries, but he is still not ready to compete.

He wrote on Instagram: 'I’m absolutely gutted. I’ve chased this dream since I was 10 years old.

'I’m not done. Stepping away from the title is not stepping away from the sport or the dream. I’ll continue doing everything I can to get healthy, get cleared and get back to competing as soon as possible.

'What makes this particularly difficult is that many of the complications I’m dealing with are a result of fouls that changed the course of my career. Fighters rely on officials to enforce the rules and protect us in those moments, and it’s hard to still be dealing with the consequences today.'

Tom Aspinall has vacated his UFC heavyweight title due to 'ongoing complications' with eyes injuries

He was diagnosed with a rare condition Brown's syndrome following an eye poke at UFC 321

He also said: 'Ongoing complications with my eyes mean I cannot get medically cleared to fight right now.

'I’ve had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing.

'I had previously agreed to a fight date and was back sparring, feeling great and ready to compete when an accident caused further damage to my right eye. This means more time away from the sport, and right now, the timing of my return is unclear.'

He added: 'I’ve now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I’ve asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don’t want to hold the heavyweight division up. I know what it’s like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title.'

Aspinall returned to training in June with a view to fighting Gane in September but the wait will have to go on.

In August, Aspinall rebuffed suggestions that he would leave the UFC.

Against Gane in October, Aspinall retained his UFC heavyweight title via no contest in an anticlimactic ending to the main event at UFC 321 that saw the Brit struggling to see and rushed to hospital.

He does intend to return to fighting in the UFC but is unable to at the moment

After four minutes of the first round of the fight in Abu Dhabi, as Aspinall attempted a kick, Gane went at his rival with a punch and inadvertently raked his fingers across his eyes. A five-minute timeout ensued, and the doctor stepped in.

Aspinall was spotted telling the doctor: 'I can't see,' with the doctor himself telling the referee that he had 'no immediate concerns about the globe'.

After four minutes of the five allocated, however, the fight was waved off as a no-contest.

'All that training for that,' Aspinall said. 'What the f*** is he doing?

'He got warned twice before it. Twice before it he got warned for it and he f***ing did it again.'

Gane, however, said: 'I didn't do it on purpose. I know what it's like to have an eye poke, because when I fought Derrick Lewis, I got an eye poke and I was seeing two of Derrick Lewis for a full round.

'During a bit of the round and the rest of the round, I saw two of Derrick Lewis. So I'm not going to say, he's a liar.'

Aspinall, who was sat with his eye strapped up, added: 'I could feel how deep it was in my eye. It feels like the back of my eyeball is hurting. It feels like someone's touched the back of my eyeball.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment 'raging' Dominic Calvert-Lewin is told by referee his goal was taken off him after team-mate's tiny deflection
Sports.content:
Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave a hilarious reaction to being told his side's second goal had been taken away from him on Monday night. The Whites thumped Newcastle 4-1 in a stellar performance at Elland Road, with four different players, ultimately, on the scoresheet for the home side. Calvert-Lewin scored the third goal, but thought he had also netted the second when he headed in from James Justin's cross. But replays showed his header came off team-mate Jayden Bogle, and the full back was officially credited with the goal. Sky cameras managed to capture the exact moment Calvert-Lewin was told the goal wasn't actually his, with his face dropping in disbelief when he was told by an official at half-time. 'The ref told me at half-time they gave it to Jayden,' he said on Sky Sports after the match. 'I didn't even know he was there as I got up early and bang. I'll take the assist.' This is the hilarious moment Dominic Calvert-Lewin (right) found out Leeds' second goal against Newcastle had actually been awarded to Jayden Bogle (left) Calvert-Lewin joked after the game that he would be looking to appeal the decision Bogle, meanwhile, said: 'I didn't know anything about it. I said to the ref I didn't fancy telling him at half-time. Even during the game he was still a bit raging. He's happy with the points though.' And the saga carried on after the game. Calvert-Lewin and Bogle posed for a snap together, with the forward writing: 'He's told me that it didn't touch him. How do I appeal this scandalous decision?' He also tagged the Premier League. Calvert-Lewin would later finish well from Tarik Muharemovic's pass, making it 3-0 to his side. Lewis Miley's own goal opened the scoring and Noah Okafor's finish made it 4-0 before Bazoumana Traore netted a late consolation. The result moved Leeds up to third in the Premier League, with Newcastle sat in 12th.

Sports.title: West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer
Sports.content:
West Ham paid tribute to their cult hero and 'gentle giant' Ludek Miklosko who has died at the age of 64.

Miklosko kept 126 clean sheets in eight years with the Hammers and is perhaps best remembered for an inspirational series of saves to deny Manchester United the title in 1995.

The popular Czech, signed from Banik Ostrava for £300,000, later returned to the club as goalkeeper coach and fans have continued to sing his name for many years.

West Ham's players held a moment of silence before training on Monday, and the club will honour him before Wednesday's Carabao Cup third round tie against Fulham.

There are also plans for a tribute at next month's Championship fixture against Queens Park Rangers, where Miklosko spent the final three years of his playing career.

'Rest in peace Ludek, our beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man,' said West Ham in a statement released on Monday.

Legendary former West Ham goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died aged 64 after a cancer battle

The much-loved Czech 'gentle giant' made 373 outings for West Ham and also played for QPR

'Ludo', left, was a hugely popular figure at West Ham and tributes have been pouring in for him

Miklosko, who won 42 international caps and represent Czechoslovakia at the World Cup in 1990, was diagnosed with cancer in 2021 and announced three years later his decision to withdraw from further treatment.

His son Martin said: 'We are heartbroken to announce the passing of my Dad Ludek, following a brave and courageous battle with cancer.

'On behalf of my Mum and my family, I would like to sincerely thank the fans and everyone at West Ham United Football Club for the kind wishes, thoughts and prayers that were sent to my Dad during his illness.

'We know that the many messages and wishes from his former team-mates and fans alike were a huge sense of comfort to him in his battle with cancer and gave him the strength to not give up and keep fighting for as long as he could.

'We are heartbroken at his loss but take huge comfort from the immense support he received from all of you, along with the knowledge that he is now at peace and no longer suffering.

'Dad simply loved West Ham United, and especially hearing his name sung loud and proud at every game. The club, and its fans, were and always will be a part of our family, so thank you all from the bottom of our hearts.'

Sports.title: Richarlison aims social media dig at Roberto De Zerbi after unhappy star was exiled by Tottenham boss - and won't even play in Carabao Cup at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Richarlison aims social media dig at Roberto De Zerbi after unhappy star was exiled by Tottenham boss - and won't even play in Carabao Cup at Liverpool

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tottenham forward Richarlison has taken aim at his manager Roberto De Zerbi after the Spurs boss rejected the chance to call him up for his side's Carabao Cup game at Liverpool.

The forward has been left out of his club's Premier League squad, but is available for selection in the League Cup.

Spurs have failed to score in their first four Premier League games this season, an embarrassment heightened by the omission of Richarlison – last season's top scorer with 12 goals – from the squad.

'Nothing changes in my project, in my idea,' said De Zerbi. 'I am sorry for the goals we didn't score, but we have the qualities to score goals.

'We are building a new project, a new team. I can't change my opinion about the players if they don't win or don't score. They are very good players.

'If we want to change from the last two seasons, we have to be stronger and believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. You can change players or change coaches, change, change, change, and nothing changes. Or you stay humble, with the right spirit to work.

Richarlison has taken aim at Roberto De Zerbi after his manager revealed he will not play the Brazilian in the League Cup

'I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.'

But Richarlison has snapped back. Taking to Instagram, he replied to an X post around De Zerbi's comments with a crying emoji, and then shared a screenshot of the post to Instagram with the caption: 'Why' with another crying emoji.

Richarlison started the league opener at Brentford, but was told he can leave before a move to Everton collapsed and links to Trabzonspor failed to turn into a move.

After he did not agree personal terms with boyhood club Vasco on Friday, he was in attendance for Spurs' goalless draw with Everton, but will remain on the sidelines.

De Zerbi, who will be without Sandro Tonali against Liverpool after the midfielder picked up a knock, took his players out to dinner last week as he did in April, after they lost at Sunderland in his first game in charge. They returned to Mediterranean restaurant Bacchanalia in Mayfair and the Spurs boss picked up the bill.

'Something to eat, some water, some beers,' said De Zerbi. 'It is a pleasure.'

De Zerbi pored over the first half-hour of Saturday's 0-0 draw with Everton to analyse why his side could not convert their dominance into goals.

'We played 25-30 minutes very well,' said De Zerbi. 'We could have scored two. We maybe lost confidence because we didn't score. We have to improve.'

Richarlison, having demanded to leave Spurs in the summer and then failed to agree personal terms with Everton, Trabzonspor or Vasco da Gama, will remain out in the cold.

'We lost at Brentford 3-0 [on the opening day] with Richarlison,' De Zerbi added. 'Maybe you forgot. Just to remind you.'

Sports.title: John McEnroe's 'unprofessional' and 'belittling' comments are slammed as the 'final straw' by angry US Open fans
Sports.content:
John McEnroe's 'unprofessional' and 'belittling' comments are slammed as the 'final straw' by angry US Open fans

ESPN is facing calls to axe John McEnroe after he controversially pleaded for Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz to return to their best in wake of Alexander Zverev's US Open win.

Zverev sealed a second Grand Slam of the year with a four-set victory over home favorite Ben Shelton on Sunday.

The No 1 seed, whose service routine has sparked calls for a rule change, broke the hearts of a New York crowd who hoped Shelton would become the first American man to win a major since 2003.

But he was beaten 6-3 7-6 5-7 6-2 by Zverev and afterwards a clip went viral from ESPN's coverage of the US Open final.

'So the drought continues but the rebirth of Sascha Zverev also continues into 2027 - Down Under awaits, huh?' lead announcer Chris Fowler said, looking ahead to the Australian Open.

'Get healthy Carlos and Jannik!' responded McEnroe, the seven-time Grand Slam singles champion who serves as an analyst alongside his brother Patrick.

This is how the commentary feed ended after the Zverev and Shelton US Open trophy ceremony.



"Get healthy Carlos and Jannik."



"Please"



😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/sUbWxJXQAa — The Tennis Letter (@TheTennisLetter) September 13, 2026

John McEnroe is facing a backlash over his comments after Alexander Zverev's US Open win

Zverev sealed a second Grand Slam of the year with a four-set victory over Ben Shelton

Both Alcaraz and Sinner have battled injury issues over recent months, with world No 1 Sinner missing the US Open with a knee problem, while Alcaraz returned at Flushing Meadows after more than four months out with wrist damage.

But McEnroe's comments sparked fury among some fans, who accused the tennis legend of being 'unprofessional' and 'belittling the sport.'

'Sorry, this should be the final straw for John McEnroe,' one supporter wrote. 'Unprofessional, belittling the sport and stealing the spotlight from the champion and runner up seconds after victory.'

Another added: 'McEnroe has to go. Carlos is healthy and he played, It's not Zverev's fault that Jannik's knee doesn't work. It's his moment and he won fair and square… this is honestly pathetic.'

Others defended the 67-year-old, however, insisting his comments were part of a discussion looking forward to the 2027 season. 'It’s exactly what most tennis fans are thinking,' one said.

It is not the first time that McEnroe has faced a backlash over comments he made at this US Open. He was earlier accused of being 'disrespectful' in the wake of Novak Djokovic's first-round exit.

After Djokovic was beaten by world No 49 Mariano Navone, McEnroe joked that the Argentine would be 'playing [his] second round on Court 21.'

Sports.title: Expert lip reader reveals what Roberto De Zerbi angrily told Mathys Tel after Tottenham's drab 0-0 draw against Everton - as goal drought rumbles on after £320m spend
Sports.content:
Expert lip reader reveals what Roberto De Zerbi angrily told Mathys Tel after Tottenham's drab 0-0 draw against Everton - as goal drought rumbles on after £320m spend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

An expert lip reader has shed light on what went on between Roberto De Zerbi and Mathys Tel during their heated conversation after Tottenham's draw with Everton.

Spurs remain winless after four games and are yet to score a goal following another drab display on Saturday against David Moyes' side.

After the match, De Zerbi approached Tel on the pitch and appeared to give him a dressing down, with the forward having struggled to make an impact after coming off the bench as a makeshift striker.

Fans have since speculated about the tense interaction, with some suggesting it hinted at signs of a falling out between the pair.

One even appeared to claim that Tel had bitten back at De Zerbi by saying: 'I was here to play football.'

However, Nicola Hickling, expert lip reader and founder of LipReader, has revealed what was actually said.

An expert lip reader has shed light on what went on between Roberto De Zerbi and Mathys Tel

The pair were involved in a heated conversation after Tottenham's 0-0 draw against Everton

Hickling claims De Zerbi said to Tel: 'You're playing like a stud,' suggesting that the forward was running around aimlessly like a horse.

In the clip, the Spurs boss can then be seen to spin, as if he was playing as a striker, with Hickling adding that he said: 'Like that. I need like that, attack focus.'

Tel is said to have replied: 'Yeah, but then I went back to play for the ball.'

Speaking after the game, De Zerbi offered further context on what had gone on, with his second comment seemingly suggesting that Tel needs to stop playing with his back to goal.

'Yes, I coached him on the pitch,' De Zerbi said in his press conference. 'The body shape of a striker. The striker can play with the shoulder on the goal.

'If we are playing with (James) Maddison, (Mohammed) Kudus and Savio, he has to play as a striker, and the striker has to look at the goal, no?

'Or on the cross of Robertson. He has to stay inside because he started (his career) as a striker. Now he's playing as a winger, but he started in his career as a striker.'

Tel was dropped to the bench for the Everton clash after De Zerbi publicly criticised his display against Nottingham Forest the week before, yet the Spurs boss insisted there were no issues between the pair of them.

He added: 'But I love Mathys as a player, as a guy. There is not a problem.'

Tottenham are back in action on Tuesday when they travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup third round, before they entertain Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: The inside story of the Manchester derby VAR error, why the haste and confusion at Stockley Park left referee Michael Oliver in the dark, the ramifications the decision could have and why it's now time to pull the plug
Sports.content:
OLIVER HOLT: The inside story of the Manchester derby VAR error, why the haste and confusion at Stockley Park left referee Michael Oliver in the dark, the ramifications the decision could have and why it's now time to pull the plug

In the build-up to the implementation of VAR in the Premier League at the start of the 2019-20 season, we chased the illusion of the perfect game, a game where officiating became less visible, a game where mistakes were never made, a game where referees faced less abuse, a game where conspiracy theories became obsolete.

So let’s call this our seven-year-itch. Because in the time that has elapsed, VAR has not had the effect that those of us who were in favour of it dearly hoped that it would.

It has had, if anything, the opposite effect. The idea VAR would help us talk more about football and less about refereeing decisions is dead. It has been dead for some time.

More and more, football is becoming less about sport. For many, including the clubs trying to find ways to ban season-ticket holders and admit high-spending day-trippers in their place, its value lies in the idea that it is an adjunct to showbiz.

The sport itself is an inconvenient distraction. And VAR has become an indispensable part of that trend.

Technology was supposed to be the gateway to better games and fewer controversies but machines, and the human beings who operate them, have limits and we have found those limits.

You want a clear and obvious error? How about this: our game spends way more time than is healthy obsessing about contentious offsides and trying to decipher laws that seem so arcane that they baffle and perplex and enrage us.

Technology was supposed to be the gateway to better games and fewer controversies but machines, and the human beings who operate them, have limits and we have found those limits

Referee Michael Oliver waits for the VAR to reveal the decision around Erling Haaland's goal in the Manchester derby

You want to know what VAR has done? It has spread the blame. Now we can scream at the referee, his two linesmen, the fourth official and the unfortunate official sitting in a room surrounded by screens at Stockley Park, trying to compute a series of questions being thrown at him by a football match and knowing that every second he delays brings the wrath of the watching public down around his ears.

Its other achievement? It has robbed the Premier League and other forms of so-called elite football of its spontaneity. It has robbed football fans of their greatest joy, which is celebrating a goal with abandon.

Abandon has been taken away from fans of top-flight clubs now because there is always, always that thought in your head that maybe you have missed something. Maybe that goal you just thought you saw wasn’t a goal after all.

We have got to a stage where even discussion of a game like Sunday’s Manchester derby, always one of the biggest fixtures in the domestic calendar, is totally dominated by VAR’s incomprehensible decision to allow Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City even though Enzo Fernandez was clearly in an offside position and clearly influenced play when he flung himself at the ball in the build-up.

It is a textbook example of how VAR has made football worse.

Michael Oliver, the on-field official at Old Trafford, is the best referee in this country and yet in VAR’s haste and confusion, in its desperation to make a decision and let play resume, it cut Oliver out of the decision-making process and did not call him to the screen so he could review the action himself.

The way the VAR system works, the on-field official is not party to the discussions going on at Stockley Park and so, as the lengthy mea culpa from ProRef appeared to admit on Sunday evening, the first Oliver would have known about the decision to overrule the original offside flag against Haaland and allow the goal to stand was when the decision was relayed to him as a fait accompli.

It appears that VAR had become so single-minded about deciding whether Haaland was offside – he wasn’t – that it totally neglected to consider the subjective decision about whether the actions of Fernandez influenced play.

Then it neglected to recommend Oliver, who would surely have ruled out the goal had he been allowed to see a replay, conduct an on-field review.

And so City, who were the better team, won the game with a goal that should not have stood. And it may be a goal with far-reaching repercussions.

City won with a goal that should not have stood, as a diving Enzo Fernandez clearly interfered with play from an offside position before Haaland scored

Maybe the two extra points City gained because of it will be critical in the outcome of this season’s title race

Michael Carrick, the Manchester United manager, is certainly under increased pressure because of it. Maybe the two extra points City gained because of it will be critical in the outcome of this season’s title race.

It was good old-fashioned human error. We don’t need VAR for human error. We are more than capable of that ourselves. VAR was supposed to eradicate human error. But it hasn’t. It has added another layer of human error.

On Sunday, the incompetence of VAR was allowed to override the excellence and experience of the match official. It was a mess. Its only redeeming feature was that it was an honest mistake.

A bit like VAR itself really. VAR was an error. More and more people are recognising that. More and more people are losing their love of the game because of it.

More and more people feel it is taking away what is most precious about the sport. I have thought this for a while now and Sunday only confirmed it: it is time for the end of the error.

There is a widespread and increasingly damaging perception that the Premier League is moving further and further away from its fanbase. There is an increasing feeling, in fact, that some of its clubs regard their fan-bases with barely-disguised contempt. If they do nothing to banish VAR, then it will be more proof of that.

It is within their power to scrap it in their own competition. Sweden's Allsvenskan operates without it. If the Premier League clubs wanted to turn their backs on it and show fans they care about them, they could vote to abandon it.

If they operated with vision or conviction or loyalty to supporters, the Premier League would do the right thing. But it won’t.

Fernandez goes for the ball, drawing Lisandro Martinez closer to him and leaving Haaland unmarked

Michael Carrick, the Manchester United manager, is under increased pressure because of the error made by the VAR

Match of the Day offers a welcome shot in the arm

In the first few weeks of this football season, I have felt in danger of becoming a statistic: one of the growing percentage of viewers turning away from Match of the Day. I have been a loyal viewer for 50 years but sometimes, it has felt as if the demise of the programme is a self-fulfilling prophecy.

Seducing the reduced-concentration generation with separate highlights packages and facing more episodes without the services of some of their best pundits is not a combination designed to boost audience. But on Sunday night, even more in need of distraction than usual after dropping off my son for his first day at university, I found refuge in it again.

It was still like turning to an old friend. Mark Chapman is as good as any presenter on television, Wayne Rooney and Danny Murphy are excellent pundits with personality and attitude and the Manchester derby yielded up a range of controversies for them to discuss.

The BBC may be trying to wean us off it but I’m not ready to let it go just yet.

Sports.title: Gary Neville picks between Arsenal and Man City after summer transfer moves
Sports.content:
Gary Neville picks between Arsenal and Man City after summer transfer moves

Gary Neville believes there is one clear favourite for the Premier League crown this season with Arsenal and Manchester City both sat on 12 points after four games

View 2 Images Gary Neville has picked between Arsenal and Man City for the Premier League (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville feels Manchester City can now run Arsenal close in the title race after a flurry of late transfer activity - but they are not quite on the level of defending champions.

‌



Mikel Arteta oversaw Arsenal's first Premier League title win for 22 years last term after finally besting Manchester City in the title race. Both sides have strengthened over the summer, although City are now under new management after Pep Guardiola decided to bring the curtain down on his trophy-laden reign in Manchester back in May.

‌



After two years away from their throne, City have reshaped their squad with big-money deals for Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi in the summer transfer window.

‌



But City have been told that Arsenal are still a better team, even though Neville feels they have closed the gap on their title rivals somewhat.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There was a point probably two or three weeks before the end of the transfer window when City didn’t have in Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez and Ndiaye that you thought they look well short, particularly in midfield," Neville told Sky Sports.

"They get those three in late on which is £250million worth of business I think and it’s transformed the look of the team."

City, like Arsenal, have a 100 per cent record in the Premier League from their opening four games after beating Manchester United in the Manchester derby on Sunday. Neville feels the availability of their experienced defenders will be crucial to any hopes City have of matching Arsenal stride for stride as the season progresses.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City have won all four of their Premier League games so far under Enzo Maresca (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

He added: "And I think the big thing for City is it’s going to come down to the defence. It’s going to come down to Dias being fit. It’s going to come down to Gvardiol being fit.

"The experienced players back there and Guehi, obviously. If you can keep that back four and you’ve got Khusanov on the bench and Nico O’Reilly, it’s a youngish back four as with some younger defenders.

‌



"If they don’t pick up injuries Manchester City they can give Arsenal a real run. I still think Arsenal are better, but City have improved enormously with the signings they made at the end of the window.

"That [beating Manchester United] was big for Maresca, to establish a big-game mentality."

Sports.title: Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning EuroMillions when epic charity runs get tough
Sports.content:
Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning EuroMillions when epic charity runs get tough

Sir Kevin Sinfield, who has raised £11million from his previous six fundraising events, describes his latest effort - seven ultramarathons in seven days - as "doing a bit of running for a mate" in Rob Burrow

Kevin Sinfield on his last MND challenge

Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning the EuroMillions when the going gets tough in his epic MND charity runs.

‌



The shy superhero has raised £11million from his previous six fundraising events. He describes his latest effort - seven ultramarathons in seven days - as "doing a bit of running for a mate". The friend is rugby league legend and Sir Kevin's former team mate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024 after living with motor neurone disease (MND) for more than four years.

‌



Dad-of-two Sir Kevin dreams of winning the lottery to fund a cure for the disease - and buy a new car for his dad Ray - in times of need. Asked how he handles the mental battle of running more than 30 miles a day, he said: "I dream of winning the EuroMillions. That is my favourite one.

‌



"It is always the same amount, my dad always gets a new car. Then we cure MND with it."

Rugby legend Kevin Sinfield finally knighted in Birthday Honours for MND fundraising heroics READ MORE :

View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield dreams of winning the lottery on his epic runs (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

Sir Kevin Sinfield launches latest MND fundraiser

Speaking at Old Trafford where he launched his last fundraiser at the SuperLeague Dream Team event, he admitted that the training "just gets harder" as you grow older.

‌



His aim is to help as many MND sufferers as possible. Rob Burrow, his former Leeds Rhinos team mate, raised more than £20m for MND research. Sir Kevin has added another £11m.

Sir Kevin told how his latest venture will help research to find a cure, and support those who have been diagnosed with the disease.

"I finished the last block of running on Saturday which was my birthday. The challenge now is to stay fit and healthy and be really smart for the next two weeks," he said.

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield carries his best friend Rob Burrow over the finishing line of the Leeds Marathon in 2023 (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

"I have not trained harder; it just gets harder and I am getting older. It would be great to find a cure, we are still a fair stretch from that. The cure is the dream for everyone involved.

"In the short term, we have to help the families diagnosed today and tomorrow. We are letting them down, and that has been the case for decades. We can help them.

‌



"Then there is the awareness because it makes such a difference when people know and understand this condition.

"Over past three and four years, at the stops in the running, we have brought people together, and that shows the love support for the MND families.

"And can share in grief for the families who have lost loved ones. I am a shy bloke; I have love for the team who have been immense through all this."

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin Sinfield is now an England rugby union coach (Image: Danny Lawson/PA Wire)

'We did this for Rob'

Asked about the secret of his success, he said they had been "incredibly lucky" with the timing of their first effort during Covid.

He added: "There were no other charity or sporting events, and people wanted to give their money, it was just incredible. I never forget why we started this - it was to run for Rob, it has always been about doing a bit of running for a mate.

‌



"I did a half marathon on Saturday and then had a recovery, and I went for a meal as most people do for their birthday. Juggling family time and work is tough for everybody preparing for a marathon. It is just the same for me."

He has just returned from South Africa where he said he was "chased by a pack of dogs" while training. He has also been to Argentina, where he was told that he might have to 'barricade himself in the hotel' in Buenos Aires during the England v Argentina World Cup semi final.

He has completed an incredible 500km of training over the past few weeks. The dad, from Oldham, Greater Manchester, has also been in touch with Jai Arrow, the forward for the South Sydney Rabbitohs, who announced his immediate retirement from the National Rugby League (NRL) in May after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) at age 30.

‌



View 5 Images Sir Kevin on his Ultra 7 challenge in 2022 (Image: PA)

'There is a war to be won against MND'

Sir Kevin is Australia next year for the rugby World Cup and 'has an idea' about doing one more charity event abroad. But he wanted to bring the curtain down on his UK exploits, with a tour of the rugby league grounds of the North at the end of this month.

"I needed to release the team, and this is something I could do," he added. "The support for Rob and the Burrow family in Leeds is always great.

‌



"I look forward to going back there thanks to my history with the city. I'm also really looking forward going back to the North West, seeing the people who have supported us.

"I know it will be an incredible week. It sounds strange given the rivalry but I always get a warm welcome in Hull and I love going there.

"All the Superleague clubs have been great, after the final on October 3 is over, and the battle is over, there is a war to be won against MND and I hope they can help with that."

‌



He admits that he still "does not like running" but added: "I makes you a better person, and a bit kinder. I would always encourage people to exercise, getting out there in the open air is so good for you, for your mental health. The good thing is that people are always nice to me now.

"Opposition clubs were always respectful to me after I retired from the game, and we have seen the best of our home nations. The fans always turn up with a big smile which is so important and the nice thing is that people don't just talk bout rugby now, they talk about running and the MND community."

View 5 Images Sir Kevin and Rob Burrow are pictured at an event in May 2023 (Image: PA)

‌



Sir Kevin, who turned 46 on Saturday, will visit all 12 English Betfred Super League grounds from Sept 27 to Oct 3 as he completes seven ultra marathons in seven days.

Now an England rugby union coach, he has already completed six epic endurance challenges for MND research. He will start at Hull Kingston Rovers on September 28 and call in at the grounds of the 11 other English top-flight rugby league clubs along the way.

The "7 in 7: The Grand Finale" venture is set to finish on the pitch at Old Trafford ahead of the Super League Grand Final. As part of his challenge, he will run a mile each day alongside people affected by the neurodegenerative illness.

Article continues below

Each day will be separated into 7 km blocks, which Sinfield has to complete within an hour. His route will take him across the Pennines on day five, and that day he will visit Wigan Warriors and Leigh Leopards.

The last run sets off at St Helens, calls at Warrington Wolves, and then heads to Manchester. You can find out full details of this year’s challenge using this link.

Sports.title: Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit
Sports.content:
Robin van Persie lands new job as ex-Man Utd ace recovers from shock managerial exit

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal ace Robin van Persie is now embarking on a new project after his first senior managerial role came to an end

View 3 Images Robin van Persie has recently started a new role (Image: 2026 BSR Agency)

Former Manchester United and Arsenal forward Robin van Persie has become a global ambassador for e-bike brand ENGWE. At the end of last season, Van Persie's managerial role with Feyenoord came to an end after 16 months.

He earned Champions League qualification with the Dutch side after finishing second in the Eredivisie but was surprisingly relieved of his duties. The ex-striker's exit took place not long after the club appointed Devy Rigaux as technical director and Robert Eenhoorn as general manager.

Now, a few months after his departure, it's been announced that the Dutchman, who scored 144 goals and contributed 59 assists in 280 Premier League appearances, will work in an ambassadorial capacity for the global e-bike brand.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

After the new role with ENGWE was announced, Van Persie said: "Throughout my career, reliability has always mattered. Being able to trust the people around you, your equipment and your decisions.

"That is one of the things that attracted me to ENGWE. Today, staying active and finding better ways to move are just as important to me.”

A spokesperson for the brand also said: " Robin represents performance, discipline and reliability, but also an active way of life that goes far beyond football.

View 3 Images Robin van Persie has become the company's latest ambassador (Image: ENGWE)

"Together, we want to make e-mobility a more natural part of everyday life and inspire more people to move, explore and enjoy every ride.”

Van Persie is yet to return to football after leaving Feyenoord, who hired his former Netherlands team-mate and ex-Rangers manager Giovanni van Bronckhorst as his successor.

He still has a firm connection to the club, with his son Shaqueel van Persie turning out for the Dutch giants. Last season, the ex-United forward was the one who gave Shaqueel his senior debut for the Rotterdam side.

View 3 Images Van Persie is yet to return to football (Image: 2026 Koji Watanabe)

When asked why he turned to his son, who is also a left-footed striker, during a 3-1 Europa League defeat to Celtic, Van Persie replied: "I made that call as a coach, not as a dad because we needed a goal.

"Shaqueel is a player who can score a goal from all angles. That was the reason I brought him on. From a father's point of view, when your son makes his debut that is always a special moment. But I wasn't that busy with enjoying that moment, I was doing my work like Shaqueel was."
