When Moody first got involved with the project in late 2012, the writer and actress Phoebe Waller-Bridge had written roughly a page.

"We really didn't know what it was yet at all," Moody said.

Waller-Bridge had been invited to put together a short monologue as part of a storytelling night at a London theater. At the time, Moody, who was already producing another play with Waller-Bridge, asked if she could read what she had written down. She immediately became hooked.

Sponsor Message

"You know when you get that fizzy feeling when you read something that you think is really exciting, and it doesn't really matter that it's not all there yet?"

That fizzy feeling was enough for Moody to secure a venue at the Fringe.

What followed was a dizzying, anxiety-soaked six-month period in which Moody, still only 26, learned two important lessons: First, trust is invaluable to the producer-artist relationship. And second, so is a hard deadline.

A week before rehearsals, Moody stopped by Waller-Bridge's house to see how she was getting on with the script. Save for a scatter of Post-It notes laid out across the floor, the play was still not written.

Moody, who by then had gained a reputation amongst colleagues for her keep-calm-and-carry-on demeanor, reassured Waller-Bridge, then locked her in a room and told her to keep writing.

toggle caption Rebecca Rosman/NPR

A colleague later found Moody hyperventilating in a closet.

"I was wondering what would happen if this play didn't get made," she said.

It did, though the final ending — at one point there were at least three alternate conclusions — was written on the train up to the festival.

The show was still rough around the edges when it arrived in Edinburgh.

Reviews were mixed — "Waller-Bridge hasn't produced a flawless piece of writing," the critic Lyn Gardner wrote in The Guardian (though she did acknowledge for all its flaws, it was "hugely distinctive").

But Moody says that lack of polish was part of the point.

"The Fringe is this place for messy, complicated, unfinished, scrappy stuff because it's those bits that you'll find the magic in," Moody says.

A different kind of stage

Moody's own relationship with the Fringe started as a compromise.

After telling her parents she wanted to become an actor, they gently suggested she try an internship on the organizational side of things — a slightly less precarious path.

Sponsor Message

She landed an internship at the Fringe, handing out flyers and moving sets around. It was her first time away from home. She says she hasn't missed a year at the Fringe since.

Years later, just out of drama school, she bumped into a friend one day at the Fringe who said he was getting into producing, and asked if she wanted to help with a project. She accepted. While the project didn't materialize into a big break, something clicked.

"I suddenly realized everything that I loved about acting, producing was actually serving that in a better way," she said. "I felt like I had way more autonomy."

Producing still kept her at the center of the creative process, but gave her a say in what got made — and how.

At 23, she put on her first show at the Fringe, a play called The Ducks, written by playwright Michael McLean. The experience catapulted Moody into not just the Fringe, but the wider London theater ecosystem, eventually leading to her big break with Fleabag in 2013.

Five years later, she launched her own company, Francesca Moody Productions.

Around the same time, a couple of friends sent her a script for Baby Reindeer, a monologue written by the Scottish actor Richard Gadd. It was based on his real life experiences with a stalker.

Enlarge this image toggle caption Netflix Netflix

Moody started reading the script on a train from Norwich to London and became so absorbed that, when the train reached the station, she stayed in her seat to finish the final pages.

She didn't know how she was going to produce it.

But, she thought, "By hook or by crook, I'm going to do it."

In 2019, Baby Reindeer premiered at the Fringe. Five years later, it became a Netflix series — and just like Fleabag, a global hit.

The success of both shows changed things for Moody, whose name has become a stamp of approval at the Fringe.

Sponsor Message

At this year's Fringe, Moody backed three very different shows: Crybabies: The Scaring, a horror sketch comedy; Roleplay, a one-woman drama about feminism, sex and the personas we build online; and Garry Starr: Classic Penguins, a raucous hour where a nearly naked Starr, reenacts a series of Penguin Classics — almost entirely naked.

For all their differences, Moody sees a common thread in the work she backs — comedy that doesn't take itself too seriously, even when the ideas underneath it do.

Roleplay, which perhaps generated the most buzz, sold out its full run before the festival had even kicked off. India Scarlet Kolb, a creative director from London, bought her tickets two-and-a-half months in advance. After the show, in the venue's courtyard, she said Moody's name was part of the appeal.

"I wanted to kind of see what the next hit of the Fringe would be," she said.

That reputation can be a gift to the artists Moody backs. It can also come with baggage, says Hannah Reilly, the star and writer of Roleplay.

toggle caption Mihaela Bodlovic

"This work will never be viewed in a vacuum," Reilly said. "There can definitely be some people approaching the work with arms folded a little bit, saying 'this better be better than Fleabag and Baby Reindeer combined.'"

"Guys," she added. "This is my first solo show. Can we just take it for what it is?"

But Reilly also says Moody's role goes beyond simply scouting good work. During the development of Roleplay, Reilly says she encouraged her to lean further into the darker parts of the story and take risks.

"She really wants you to make the boldest version of what's in your head," Reilly said.

And despite the reputation, not every bet pays off for Moody.

In 2023, she produced Berlusconi: A New Musical, a satirical comedy about the former Italian Prime Minister that became a commercial and critical flop.

But that, Moody says, is part of the bargain.

"I try really, really hard not to think too much about what's coming down the line," she said.

Developing a show with a future television adaptation in mind "just isn't great for storytelling."

Take Garry Starr, one of Moody's other productions, which made its New York debut earlier this month.

toggle caption Colin Hattersley/Premier Comms

The premise is hardly mainstream TV material: Garry Elizabeth Starr, the alter ego of Australian clown Damien Warren-Smith, realizes that books, just like penguins, are on the brink of extinction. Thus begins the inspiration for his journey to save penguins and literature at the same time, by acting the titles of a series of Penguin Classics books in front of a live audience.

Sponsor Message

On top of that, he's naked (save for a pair of penguin flippers, a tuxedo jacket and a black top hat). To pull it all off, Starr also needs plenty of help from the audience — and, perhaps most surprisingly — they are more than willing to play along.

Moody saw the production at the Fringe two years ago, and loved it enough to sign on as a producer.

"It's completely non-political," Warren-Smith said. "It's pure escapism."

And maybe that's what Moody is really betting on. Not the next Fleabag or Baby Reindeer.

Just something strange enough — and true enough — to be worth the risk.

World.title: What we know about Carney's push for a 'unique alliance' with the EU
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday that Canada plans to begin discussions on a "unique alliance" with the European Union.

Carney was responding to a Wall Street Journal article that said Canada was seeking to become an "associate member" of the 27-nation bloc.

That report included this quote from Finnish President Alexander Stubb: "Wouldn’t it be lovely if Canada was the 28th state of the European Union rather than the 51st state of the United States?"

In response to the article, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre and other MPs in his party said on X on Sunday that Canadians should be concerned about becoming the "28th EU state."

Here is what we know about the Canada-EU partnership as Carney prepares to deliver a speech to the European Parliament on Thursday morning.

Is Canada planning to join the EU?

No, Carney says. The prime minister reiterated at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sunday that that is not the plan.

"We're not looking to become a member of the European Union," Carney said, adding that officials are instead looking to begin discussions on a "unique alliance."



"We share the same values, we have the same priorities, and we have very complementary strengths," he said.

WATCH | See Carney's comment here: Canada looking into 'unique alliance' with EU, not membership: Carney | Duration 0:33 Prime Minister Mark Carney was asked on the red carpet of the Toronto International Film Festival about a Wall Street Journal report that suggested he was exploring whether Canada could become an 'associate member' of the European Union. He said Canada plans to begin discussions for a 'unique alliance' with the bloc, but will not seek membership.

Has the idea of full EU membership been floated?

Not officially, but the idea has made the rounds among media and some people in power as Canada seeks to become less dependent on its relationship with the U.S.

One public instance was a comment by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, who said in March that "maybe Canada at some point" could 

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, shown in Helsinki on Monday, casually floated the idea of Canada joining the EU in March. (Mikko Stig/Lehtikuva/The Associated Press)

Barrot's comments at a European conference in Berlin generated laughs and applause at the time, though Carney has consistently said, as early as June 2025, that membership is not on the table.

He said then that he wants to "co-operate much more clearly and broadly to our mutual benefit."



"Not as a member, but along that continuum."

What is an 'associate' member?

Saturday's Wall Street Journal article said Carney is pushing his team to take Ottawa's relationship with the EU "to the next level" — including having Canada take on a new title: "Associate Member of the European Union."

"Associate member" is not a legal designation.

A senior Canadian official, who offered information to CBC News on a not-for-attribution basis, said the "associate member" label is one of a few that have been considered and that Canada did not propose it.

The official added that the government is still examining what the relationship could look like, and hopes to more clearly sketch it out at the EU-Canada summit at the end of October.

The official said they did a deep analysis of the EU's relationships with non-members Norway, Switzerland, the U.K. and Georgia and said none of those would work because the Canadian government does not want to give up independence in return for access.

What do we know about deepening ties between the EU and Canada?

Carney and the EU's ambassador to Canada, Geneviève Tuts, have both used the same word: "unique."

But there have been few on-the-record details beyond a willingness on both sides to work something out.



Carney said on Aug. 22 that the two sides would talk this fall about building a "much stronger and deeper" security and economic partnership. This is on top of their only partially applied free-trade deal (CETA) and the non-trade Strategic Partnership Agreement, as well as the Security and Defence Partnership they signed in June 2025.

Tuts said what that looks like is still being worked out.

WATCH | Canada should increase trade, Dion says: Canada will 'not become a member of the EU,' Stéphane Dion says | Duration 1:21 Former Liberal leader and Special Envoy to the European Union Stéphane Dion says the idea of Canada joining the EU 'will never happen,' but Canada must look to increase trade with the EU above eight per cent. Conservatives and Liberals 'should all agree it's the thing we need to do,' he added.

The Wall Street Journal report says Canada and the EU are "eyeing ways" for Canada to move closer on energy, AI, critical minerals and defence.

The Canadian official said they're aiming for more options on where Canadians study, travel, do business and retire.

What are the possibilities?

Tuts said she expects only discussions about any new partnership at this point, possibly with more detail from speeches by Carney on Thursday and by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday.

Achim Hurrelmann, co-director of the Centre for European Studies at Carleton University, says it seems the new agreement is being put together in a hurry.

He said the plan might include things like collaboration on a European stockpile of critical minerals, university student exchanges through the Erasmus program and a digital trade agreement.

Hurrelmann said this all might amount to a series of agreements instead of a major pact, or a grab bag of ideas assembled under the label of "co-operating on strategic capabilities."

"There are lots of initiatives, but they don’t at this point really amount, from what I can see, to this systematically new step in the relationship," he said. "I’m not really sure if the substance will actually justify the new label."

World.title: 'Cool to be Canadian': Leaders optimistic their pitch to invest here will pay off
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Canada is a safe and competitive place to do business, teeming with hundreds of capital-ready major projects to pour dollars into — at least, that's the pitch Canadian business leaders and politicians are in the midst of making to some of the world's top money managers.

And as this week's Canada Investment Summit kicks off, there's plenty of optimism on the Canadian side that investors are starting to see the country that way.

The multi-day summit is bringing financiers from abroad responsible for managing trillions of dollars worth of capital to Toronto, where they'll be pitched on major Canadian projects.

Led by the Prime Minister Mark Carney, the exclusive summit is set to feature a Monday night dinner at the Art Gallery of Ontario, talks from high-profile Canadian business leaders and closing remarks from former prime minister Stephen Harper.

The list of invitees spans Canadian business leaders, foreign investors and politicians past and present. Chief executive of investment bank Barclays C.S. Venkatakrishnan, Blackstone president and CEO Jon Gray, president and CEO of CIBC Harry Culham, and head of OpenAI for Countries George Osborne are among them.

On the political side, National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak, CEO of the government's Major Projects Office Dawn Farrell and former Canadian prime minister Jean Chrétien will also attend.

WATCH | Carney hosts investment summit amid trade war: Carney hosts investment summit amid trade war | Duration 2:44 Prime Minister Mark Carney is hosting a two day investment summit in Toronto in an attempt to attract foreign capital to the country amid an escalating trade war with the United States.

Though foreign investors haven't always viewed Canada as the best place to pour their money, Goldy Hyder, president and CEO of the Business Council of Canada, says that attitude is changing.

"It's really cool to be Canadian right now. People I've been meeting with are excited about what they're hearing and what they're seeing," Hyder said.

The government has already made moves aimed at showing they're serious about building big things, too.

Minister of Finance François-Philippe Champagne on Monday announced the Canadian Revenue Agency will prioritize advanced income tax rulings for investments over $1 billion.

The program, which goes into effect immediately, will allow investors to know how income tax law will apply to a proposed investment before they commit money to it, reducing risk, according to a government release.

"When investors are considering major projects, certainty matters," Champagne said.

Companies see changes

In recent years, long turnaround times for major projects and uncertainty about whether or not projects will get approved have hurt Canada's reputation in the eyes of investors, business leaders say.

A recent report by the CPP Investment Insights Institute collected responses from global investors and found that while Canada ranked high in terms of stability, regulatory complexity and permitting timelines were big concerns, especially among energy and mining projects — the areas where investors saw some of the most value in Canada.

But provincial and federal governments seem to be working better with the private sector to clear the way for big projects, Hyder said, and bringing Indigenous nations on board with new projects.

Mark Selby, CEO of Canada Nickel Company, has seen the change from within, too.

He says changes to the permitting process have helped his company secure key federal permits for the Crawford nickel project, which is included in the government's pitchbook for the summit, in about half the time it would have taken previously.

That 66-page pitchbook obtained by CBC News last week listed more than 160 projects that will be on the table at the summit, 11 of which were listed as shovel ready and about two dozen more in an advanced stage.

Frank McKenna, deputy chair at TD Securities and former Canadian ambassador to the U.S., said many of the projects are "fully baked" opportunities ready for financing, which could help meet the moment for investors.

WATCH | McKenna says Canada proving to investors its a trustworthy place to invest: Prime minister's investment summit 'breathtakingly audacious': former ambassador | Duration 9:34 As the world's richest investors head to Toronto next week, former Canadian ambassador to the U.S. Frank McKenna tells Power & Politics that Prime Minister Mark Carney's investment summit is 'more audacious and more ambitious' than previous government attempts to attract foreign investment, especially at a time when investors are looking for reliability in the face of global uncertainty.

And while Canada finds itself in a moment of trade upheaval with the U.S., which some have worried could make Canada look less stable, McKenna points out the rest of the world is going through that upheaval in tandem — which could work in Canada's favour.

"We represent those other options, and we represent a country with a well-developed rule of law and stability," McKenna told CBC's Power & Politics on Friday.

"All of that makes us an attractive … alternative place to invest."

Deals could take time

Selby is seeking $2 billion to help fund the Crawford mining project included in the prospectus, but he's not expecting to walk away from the two-day event with it in hand.

"The summit for most mining companies is really a door-opener," Selby said.

Mark Selby, CEO of Canada Nickel Company, says the government's work to make Canada more attractive to businesses is working. (Abby Hughes/CBC)

He says some of the really big international investors likely won't be looking to put their money in projects that only need a few billion, like his. Still, he says the attention of the prime minister will make Canadian industries including mining more attractive, and will open more doors for the future.

Minister of Industry Mélanie Joly said she was hopeful "good deals" and memorandums of understanding pledging future investment will come out of the summit, though the full impact of those deals might only be apparent in time.

"What I'm hearing and based on many of the conversations I've had, it's a great momentum," Joly said. "We will see the impacts of this summit in three months, in six months, in a year."

New Brunswick Premier Susan Holt echoed the message, saying the meetings happening at the summit are like a "first date."

"You're getting to know someone, making sure that they're marriage material and they're doing the same with us," Holt said.

She says success will come in the form of follow-up meetings that lead to deals on paper.

World.title: Former Saskatoon private school admin, pictured with paddle in 1997, testifies at former principal's trial
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A photo of a former administrator for a Saskatoon private Christian school holding a wooden paddle, published in Maclean's magazine 30 years ago, is now evidence in the assault trial of a former principal at the school.

Duff Arthur Friesen faces five counts of assault with a weapon. He has pleaded not guilty to all of them.

Friesen is accused of hitting students with a wooden paddle. The charges stem from his time at Christian Centre Academy from 1997 to 2007.

The school was later renamed Legacy Christian Academy, then Valour Academy. It's closely associated with Mile Two Church, now called Encounter Church.

Duff Arthur Friesen makes his way into Saskatoon Court of King's Bench last week for the start of his jury trial. He faces five counts of assault with a weapon. (Travis Reddaway/CBC)

Lou Brunelle, the man in the magazine photo from 1997, was the first defence witness at the trial. He testified Monday that paddling was school policy and parents signed off.

Brunelle worked at the school from 1989 to 2001, first as a supervisor and then an administrative assistant, reporting to the director and senior to the teachers. He said the role can be compared to that of a vice-principal.

He said the paddle was one of multiple methods, alongside things like demerits and detentions, that the school used to enforce discipline for things like stealing, lying or cheating.

“We would chat with the child. If warranted — three swats,” he told the jury.

He said the student and the discipliner would then pray together.

Brunelle also testified that none of the staff at the school at the time were certified to work as teachers. He added that the curriculum was approved and that students received Ministry of Education transcripts that allowed them to go on to university.

Crown witnesses

The Crown closed its case Friday after calling five former students, each of whom testified about being struck with a wooden paddle.

Robyn Mandell said Friesen spanked her hard enough to leave bruises for days. She said it was extremely "humiliating, shameful and terrifying."

Coy Nolin, who testified on Wednesday, told the jury he was called to Friesen's office during a school day after Friesen sent a letter to his mother about his schoolwork, and was told he would be taken off the basketball team if he didn't catch up.

He said Friesen told him he’d be getting paddled and sent back to class. Nolin said he then put his hands on the seat of a chair and bent over.

“He struck me three times,” Nolin said.

The trial is set for two weeks, with Justice Daryl Labach presiding.

World.title: Red carpet looks from the 2026 Emmy Awards
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Stars of the small screen have begun arriving at the 78th Emmy Awards, stopping to pose on the red carpet, which is actually blue this year, a nod to the 100th anniversary of the host network, NBC, and its stylized peacock logo.

The event, which recognizes excellence in television, is taking place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angele and will be hosted by actor Mariska Hargitay.

The show will include a special musical tribute to Dolly Parton led by Reba McEntire and an in memoriam performance of Bridge Over Troubled Water by Noah Kahan. The ceremony will also celebrate the 30th anniversary of Buffy the Vampire Slayer and the 50th anniversary of Charlie’s Angels.

Some Emmys have already been handed out at the Creative Arts Emmys earlier this month, but the list of stars taking the stage tonight is quite impressive: Dan Levy, John Mulaney, Awkwafina, Shailene Woodley, Alan Cumming, Florence Pugh and Annie Murphy are just a few of the confirmed presenters.

Here are the best looks so far.

We will be updating this post throughout the evening, so check back regularly for more looks.

Supriya Ganesh

The Pitt actor Supriya Ganesh wore a pale blue gown with ruffle details and a sheer underlayer.

Matty Matheson

The Canadian chef and co-star/executive producer of The Bear wore a tailored brown-and-black tuxedo with a classic white shirt.

Lisa Rinna

Former The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills star Rinna, who appears in Season 4 of Traitors, wore a sculptural, asymmetrical black gown by Lever Couture.

Grace Gummer

The Love Story actor, who walked the red carpet with husband, Mark Ronson, wore a black pleated column dress by Dior with a standout collar necklace.

Joy Sunday

Sunday, nominated for her work in DTF St. Louis, wore an off-white embellished gown with a train and thigh-high slit.

Noah Kahan

The singer-songwriter, who will be performing at tonight’s Emmys, wore a sharp black tuxedo by Bode with colourful lapel pins and a ribbon bow tie.

World.title: Republican Mitch McConnell returns to U.S. Senate after 3-month absence
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky returned to the U.S. Senate on Monday for the first time since June 14, when he was hospitalized after a fall in his home.

McConnell's three-month absence from the Senate generated a flood of criticism and online speculation, as the Kentucky senator initially remained quiet for weeks about his condition. The 84-year-old senator eventually disclosed that he had been "briefly unconscious" due to the fall and had also been treated for mild pneumonia in the hospital.

He briefly addressed reporters from his wheelchair outside the Senate chamber ahead of the vote, smiling but speaking slowly and with some difficulty. McConnell joked that he wasn't sure how many reporters would be there after dodging so many questions during his almost two decades as leader.

He said he was back in the Senate to work on a pending farm bill and because he has an ongoing interest in NATO and "backing up our good friends who are totally in the fight against the Russians."

Journalists were told not to take video of McConnell speaking outside the Senate Chamber Monday. (Evan Vucci/Reuters)

No video allowed

Reporters and photographers were told by Senate staff not to take video of his remarks in the second-floor hallway, even though video is often permitted in that area. Still images were allowed.

In a statement issued before his remarks, McConnell said, "my recovery has been a long and often frustrating process, and the lingering effects of childhood polio haven't made it any easier."

He went on to write, "I'm still not quite back to 100%, but I've assured Leader [John] Thune that, as I continue with physical therapy on the advice of my doctors, I will do my best to be present for tough votes when our Conference needs me."

The concerns over McConnell's absence highlighted increasing public concern about the age of lawmakers and their capacity to carry out their duties. Speculation about his condition grew so intense at one point that Kentucky's Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear took the extraordinary step of issuing a public letter asking McConnell to update the public in a "transparent manner."

WATCH | McConnell's July message: Mitch McConnell confirms he's alive; his absence, death of other senator complicate Republican power | Duration 4:43 U.S. Sen. Mitch McConnell addressed speculation regarding his recent hospitalization, sharing that he suffered a fall last month that caused him to lose consciousness. McConnell’s absence, combined with the death of South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham, has created uncertainty in the U.S. Senate.

McConnell's absence was also felt over the summer as Republicans were unable to advance a farm bill out of committee. His return could give Republican leaders a needed vote as they try to advance legislation on cryptocurrency regulation and college sports.

McConnell, who holds the distinction of being the longest-serving Senate leader, is in his final months of his four decades in office. He is retiring at the end of January after one of the most consequential careers in modern politics.

Republicans have nominated U.S. Rep. Andy Barr to replace him, while Democrats have nominated former state lawmaker Charles Booker. McConnell said he is determined to finish out his term.

History of health problems

McConnell had polio in his early childhood and has long acknowledged difficulty as an adult in walking and climbing stairs.

The physician's office in Congress in the July statement said McConnell has "experienced several falls through the year" due to his "post-polio condition." The office said his physical therapy was aimed at reducing the risk of him falling again.

"A comprehensive evaluation by a multidisciplinary team determined that he had no fractures, cardiac abnormalities, stroke, tumor, or hemorrhage," the physician's office said.

McConnell was first elected to the Senate in 1984 and was the Republican leader from 2007 until last year , serving as both majority and minority leader during that period. He has remained active as a rank-and-file senator, showing up for work when the chamber is in session, often using a wheelchair to get around.

But the senator's physical condition has visibly declined in recent years.

He was hospitalized with a concussion in March 2023 and missed several weeks of work after falling in a Washington hotel.

He twice froze up during news conferences after he returned, staring vacantly ahead before colleagues and staff. A year later, he fell and sprained his wrist while walking out of a Republican luncheon.

World.title: Sydney Sweeney's 'sexualized' sports betting ad slammed by Canadian athletes
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

U.S. actor Sydney Sweeney is once again facing backlash over an .

This time, she has enraged female athletes around the world with a nude sports gambling ad — and her response.

The ad for Novig, a peer-to-peer prediction exchange focused exclusively on sports, was posted online Sept. 9 and viewed nearly 39 million times by Monday morning. It features Sweeney holding various pieces of sports equipment in front of what looks like her otherwise naked body, as bass music plays in the background.

"Think you know sports? Prove it," says the star of Euphoria and The Housemaid at the beginning of the ad as she holds a football in front of each breast.

In other shots, she perches on a basketball net while spinning a ball with only her hair covering her, holds a football in front of her pelvis, lies nude on a bench with a soccer ball resting on her feet and swings a golf club wearing only white underwear.

It set off a backlash from female athletes and Olympians who say the ad sexualizes women in sport and sets them back. The criticism crosses borders and a range of sports, with many posting "Dear Sydney Sweeney" videos on social media in response.

It also elicited a strong response from a number of Canadian athletes.

"Dear Sydney Sweeney, this is women in sports," Canadian sprint canoeist Sophia Jensen posted on TikTok on Sunday, alongside a video where the world champion competes on the water and trains in the gym.

"Hey Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Canadian figure skater Madeline Schizas posted on Instagram with a similar video where she competes and trains on and off the ice.

Canadian high diver Molly Carlson posted that "this one hits close to home." She wrote on Instagram that she spent years struggling with how her body looked in sport, "because I didn’t think I looked like the athlete I was 'supposed' to be."

"Young girls deserve to grow up seeing female athletes celebrated for their strength, courage, talent and what their bodies are capable of," she wrote alongside a video where she dives out of a helicopter.

Canada's Molly Carlson dives at the World Aquatics Championships in Singapore, Thursday, July 24, 2025. Carlson is among the Canadian athletes who have spoken out again Sydney Sweeney's sports betting ad. (Vincent Thian/The Associated Press)

Canadian gymnast Ellie Black added her voice to the throng, quoting the ad in her Instagram post — "Think you know sports? Prove it." — with a video where she flips and flies through competitions and lifts weights in the gym.

"This is women’s sport: powerful, skilled, courageous and so much more interesting than being treated as something to look at," Black wrote.

"Let’s celebrate the athletes, the work and the sport itself."

Global response from athletes

Athletes from around the world had their say, too.

"IDK what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what a woman in sport looks like," posted U.S. gymnast Gracie Kramer over a similar montage.

British sprinter Amy Hunt got a word in during a post-race interview on Sunday, after she finished fourth in the 200-metre final at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest.

" Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt told BBC Sport, adding "h ard work, blood, sweat, tears."

Australian swimmer Ariarne Titmus, the reigning Olympic champion in the 400-metre freestyle, called the ad "a kick in the face" on Instagram.

"H ow do we live in a world where monetizing a woman's body and sexualizing women's sport is still a thing?" she said, according to Australia's ABC News.

Novig CEO and co-founder Jacob Fortinsky praised the brand campaign for highlighting a platform that's "singularly focused on sports."

"Sydney helped bring that message to life in a way that’s impossible to ignore," Fortinsky said in a press release the same day the ad launched.

In the same press release, Sweeney called the campaign "a fun idea" that "brings that idea to life with confidence, humour and a playful edge."

Sydney Sweeney poses for photographers at the Armani beauty event during the Venice Film Festival on Sept. 3, 2026. (Scott A Garfitt/Invision/The Associated Press)

Not her 1st controversial ad

If this is sounding familiar, Sweeney faced similar backlash last year over an American Eagle  that was criticized for promoting white standards of beauty at best, and eugenics at worst.

In the ad, Sweeney makes a play on words between jeans (the clothing item) and genes (the genetic material).

“Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair colour, personality and even eye colour. My jeans are blue,” Sweeney said in the ad.

Some internet commentators read the ad as alluding to eugenics. Eugenics is a discredited idea that the human race could be improved by selectively breeding for certain traits.

At the time, the blond-haired, blue-eyed actor stood by the ad and downplayed the reaction, which included support from U.S. President Donald Trump, who called it the "HOTTEST ad out there."

Sweeney appeared to take a more overt approach to the backlash against her new ad, posting a series of photos on Instagram on Sunday that showed magazine covers with male and female athletes posing in little to no clothing.

WATCH | What Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle ad says about marketing: What Sydney Sweeney's American Eagle ad says about the brand's marketing | Hanomansing Tonight | Duration 6:07 Morgan Westcott, a marketing professor at the British Columbia Institute of Technology, says the American Eagle ad does not signal a 'shift,' but rather reflects a 'recycled concept' and a clear call to their target market.

This move prompted even more backlash. Canadian alpine skier Cassidy Gray called it "idiotic" and "senseless."

"It's not a joke when your life is actually you being a female athlete, and you being sexualized or not taken seriously and not given the same opportunities, and then you see one of the most famous actresses in the world going and completely wiping away all the work that you have done to be taken seriously," Gray posted in an emotional video on TikTok.

Gray also responded to those who might say it's just a commercial and not meant to be taken so seriously.

"I fear you're just out of touch, because it really is that deep."

Female athletes have historically been marketed in an over-sexualized manner, with a greater focus on t heir appearance than their skills.

This also extends to sports coverage, with women at the Tokyo 2021 Olympics 10 times more likely to be "visually objectified" with a camera angle than men, according to a report from The Representation Project . Researchers defined visual objectification as when a camera panned across an athlete's body or focused on a specific body part in a sexualizing way.

The same study found female athletes were more likely to be infantilized by commentators, often called "young ladies" and "girls."

Another recent study from World Athletics found that female athletes were consistently targeted by online abuse more than their male counterparts at four global sporting events, including the 2024 Paris Olympics.

World.title: Music festival apologizes after Flo Rida uses alcohol props at sober event in Thunder Bay, Ont.
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The Wake the Giant Music Festival is facing backlash after Grammy-nominated headliner Flo Rida used alcohol props on stage at the sober event in Thunder Bay, Ont., on Saturday.

The annual festival, which was launched in 2019, raises awareness to create a safe, inclusive environment for hundreds of Indigenous youth from remote northern communities who attend school in the city.

CBC Thunder Bay reached out to the Wake the Giant Musical Festival for comment, and was referred to a statement it released on social media on Sunday .

The statement said the festival's team apologizes and acknowledges the harm done by the American rapper's performance.

“The props used were not approved by organizers and we clearly communicated to the artist’s team that this was a sober event and that alcohol is not permitted on our stage,” the statement said.

The team also said it shared in the “hurt and disappointment” that many people felt, and wanted to assure the public that this performance does not align with the values of Wake the Giant or the Northern Nishnawbe Education Council, an Indigenous-run education authority.

“We take responsibility for booking the artist and we will take the lessons learned from this experience to ensure our core values will be at the forefront in choosing artists in the future,” the statement said.

Superior Morning 8:27 Sarah Law: Wake The Giant 2026 Recap The seventh annual Wake the Giant Music Festival took place in Thunder Bay over the weekend.Hear more about the meaning behind the movement, which aims to support Indigenous students in the city.

Other performers at the festival included the American group the Wallflowers, featuring Jakob Dylan, Bob Dylan's son, and Tia Wood, a Cree and Salish pop singer-songwriter from Canada.

A ‘very shocking’ performance

Esther Maud, a city resident who was in the VIP section during the performance, attended to show her support for the event, and for her son and his youth drum group, Charging Thunder, which opened the event.

Maud said it might have helped if she had relistened to his music to reflect on what it means and whether she should support it.

“I just went in thinking and being excited that I get to see someone in person that I kind of grew up listening to. So it didn’t even dawn on me what he represents, and what he sings and puts into his music at all."

Maud said she's going into six years of sobriety from alcohol. She said her mind was blown the moment she saw the first alcohol bottle on the stage during the show, in a space she has grown to love because it’s an alcohol- and drug-free event, and more bottles kept coming.

She could only think about people who are in early recovery or not as strong, and children thinking about what’s going on and if it was normal behaviour, Maud said.

Shortly after Flo Rida performed his third song, Maud left with her family and a friend.

If she were an organizer of the event, she said, “I probably would have put out the message to maybe the security and asked them to come and help us — tell them that we need to remove the bottles off the stage or ... get somebody to maybe do a little pause, and then quickly regroup and let him know that this is not the place for that."

Flo Rida, shown carrying two alcohol bottles, was the headliner at the festival Saturday. (Nicky Shaw/CBC News)

Maud said she appreciated the music festival's efforts in the wake of Flo Rida's controversial performance, and understood they had communicated to him what the event is about.

But she said the apology could have been better, as the performance was “really heavy and very triggering for a lot of people.”

Maud said she isn't angry at the festival itself and hopes what happened serves as a learning experience.

“I’m disappointed. I’m upset that this happened, but at the same time, I don’t want this one event and this performer to ruin everything else that they work so hard to do."

Organizers still have a chance to continue this work, she said, noting that she still wants to support them no matter what, as she sees their vision and knows how important it is.

“There are so many purposes and reasons to why this festival still needs to go and keep the momentum for the youth."

World.title: Iconic winter X Games comes to Calgary
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The iconic X Games action sports competition is coming to Calgary in February next year.

WinSport's Canada Olympic Park will host the three-day competition beginning Feb. 19, and the city will also see international musical acts Levity and Steve Aoki perform as part of the event.

The Calgary stop marks the first time in the 31-year history of the X Games that the competition will be hosted in Canada.

“X Games is one of those events you dream of hosting in your city,” said Tourism Calgary president and CEO Alisha Reynolds. “There is truly no better city than Calgary to host this electrifying event.”

The event will see some of the world's top skiers and snowboarders compete in events like Big Air, Knuckle Huck, Slopestyle and Superpipe.

Officials estimate roughly 15,000 to 20,000 spectators will attend the three days of competition.

Reynolds estimates the event will bring in roughly $25 million for the city’s visitor economy.

Canadian athletes excited to host

Calgarian Brendan Mackay, a freestyle skier with Team Canada, is excited to have the event come to his hometown. Mackay remembers what a podium finish at his first X Games in 2020 meant for his career.

“That was honestly for me a huge career-defining moment,” said Mackay. “That really set into motion what has been a really great athletic career since then.”

Growing up watching the games on TV inspired Mackay, and he says hosting could have an even bigger impact on the next generation.

Historically Aspen, Colo., has hosted many of the winter X Games events and therefore produced some of the sports' best athletes, says Mackay.

“So I think having that come to Calgary will be so impactful on all the young kids who get to go out and watch it,” he said.

WATCH | Breaking down Brendan Mackay's bronze-medal run at the Olympics: Mike Atkinson breaks down Brendan Mackay's bronze-medal run in men's freeski halfpipe | Duration 0:59 Mike Atkinson analyzes Brendan Mackay’s bronze-medal run in the men’s freeski halfpipe, breaking down the technical tricks and execution that earned him a spot on the Olympic podium.

Professional snowboarder Craig McMorris, who grew up in Saskatchewan and credits monthly trips to Canada Olympic Park for his success, is also excited for the event to finally come to Canada.

“Canada has exported the best action sports talent in the entire world — full stop,” McMorris said. "It’s finally now our time to host the X Games.”

New format for Calgary X Games

In 2026, the X Games launched a new league format where athletes compete individually but also earn points for club teams, adding a championship race that fans can follow throughout the season.

At the X Games Calgary media event on Monday, CEO Jeremy Bloom also unveiled the four clubs for the winter league, which will draft athletes later this week. They include X Games Club Whistler.

“So Canadians will have a club to root for,” Bloom said.

World.title: Colombia’s social organizations and labor unions announce national strike in November
World.content:
Some 1,500 representatives of social organizations and labor unions agreed to begin organizing an anti-government national strike that should take place throughout Colombia either on November 11 or on November 20.

The organizations agreed to the mass mobilization during the National Gathering for the Defense of Life, Dignity, Democracy, Peace, Sovereignty, and Social Reforms that had been organized by labor unions in the capital Bogota.

The first and fundamental decision of the Meeting is to declare the most radical opposition to the illegitimate government of Abelardo de la Espriella because of the course it has imposed on the country—one of subordination to the interests of U.S. imperialism and alignment with the agenda of the international far right—which constitutes a direct threat to national sovereignty, democracy, and the rights won by the Colombian people, and an undeniable shift toward fascism. Social organizations and labor unions

In a statement, the organizations said that the national strike will be preceded by regional protests on October 10 and 14 that will seek to generate momentum for the national strike.

Indigenous organizations will additionally organize a Day of Indigenous, Afro and Popular Resistance on October 12.

A final date for the national strike has yet to be defined.

The organizations decided to call a strike to protest the government’s security and defense policy, the ending of peace processes with illegal armed groups and in defense of social reforms that had been implemented by former President Gustavo Petro.

The protests additionally seek to express solidarity with the people of Palestine, western Sahara, Iran, Bolivia and Venezuela, and reject US imperialism in the Americas.

We must categorically reject the interference of U.S. government officials in the formulation of domestic policies under the guise of so-called friendly aid, which in reality masks the ambition to intensify overexploitation, extractivism, territorial control, and the presence of foreign troops on our soil. Social organizations and labor unions

The organizations agreed to “prepare, through the most intense and massive agitation and propaganda campaign, a national strike.”

World.title: Judge suspends Colombia’s aerial fumigation pilot
World.content:
A Putumayo from the southern Putumayo province suspended the government’s announced resumption of the aerial spraying of coca, ordering information that would allow “a sufficiently informed decision on the merits.”

Earlier this week, the National Narcotics Council (CNE) ordered the National Police to restart the aerial fumigation of coca, the base ingredient for cocaine, “as a controlled, limited, temporary, and evaluable experimental phase, the implementation of a pilot plan for the eradication of illicit crops through aerial spraying using a manned aircraft and the formulated product Glufosinate Ammonium 200 SL.”

The National Police subsequently said that the 10km2 pilot area was located in Putumayo, a province inside the Amazon forest.

These announcements triggered a local foundation to sue the administration, claiming that the plans to do a pilot were in violation of the 2015 ban on aerial fumigation and threatened both locals and the environment.

The judge agreed and ordered the administration of President Abelardo de la Espriella to provide information on the environmental and health risk involved in the aerial spraying with glufosinate ammonium.

The potential implementation of the pilot plan before gathering and analyzing the studies, documents, and technical evidence cited by the administration itself as the basis for the decision could render the requested constitutional protection ineffective and jeopardize the possibility of reaching a sufficiently informed decision on the merits; Indeed, the combination of the announced imminence of the measure, the current lack of essential information needed to understand its territorial, social, and environmental scope, and the particular ecological sensitivity of the department of Putumayo necessitates preventive action aimed at preserving the effectiveness of this constitutional action. Putumayo court

The suspension of the aerial spraying comes days after De la Espriella promised US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that he would resume aerial fumigation, a notoriously ineffective way to get rid of coca.

World.title: Colombia announces new aerial fumigation pilot program
World.content:
Colombia’s National Narcotics Council (CNE) ordered the National Police to restart the aerial fumigation of coca, the base ingredient for cocaine.

In a resolution, the CNE ordered “as a controlled, limited, temporary, and evaluable experimental phase, the implementation of a pilot plan for the eradication of illicit crops through aerial spraying using a manned aircraft and the formulated product Glufosinate Ammonium 200 SL.”

In a public statement, the National Police’s counternarcotics unit said that the 10km2 pilot area was located in Putumayo and would not affect indigenous and afro-descendant communities, who would need to be asked permission.

The exclusion of environmental protection zones and protected areas, zones associated with bodies of water, rivers, and other environmentally sensitive areas is contemplated, as well as those territories that, in accordance with current regulations and the corresponding technical studies, must be excluded. National Police Counternarcotics

The purpose of the pilot program is to “evaluate the effectiveness of aerial spraying, as well as its application under the established technical and operational conditions, said the police.

The police stressed that “this experimental phase does not constitute the resumption, adoption, or definitive authorization of a widespread or nationwide aerial spraying program,” which was banned by the Constitutional Court in 2015.

In order to resume aerial fumigation, health and environmental authorities must sign off on the program and the police would only be allowed to use airplanes with the approval of the court and local communities.

President Abelardo de la Espriella vowed to resume aerial spraying more than 330,000 hectares while on campaign and after taking office last month as part of his hardline approach to organized crime.

Former President Ivan Duque also vowed to resume aerial spraying, but failed to comply with the norms established by the court.

World.title: Court orders Colombia’s government to remove images of slain “narcoterrorists”
World.content:
A Bogota judge ordered Colombia’s government to remove images and videos of President Abelardo de la Espriella walking through the remains of slain suspected guerrillas from its social media accounts.

The judge also ordered the government to remove images and videos of the body bags containing the lifeless remains of four members of organized crime group ACSN who were killed in La Guajira.

According to the judge, the images could be harmful to minors.

The decision was celebrated by congressman Santiago Osorio (Green Alliance), who sued the government over the controversial social media posts.

The State and the National Government cannot engage in a contest with crime to see which of the two is the most cruel; in this regard, the Office of the President of the Republic, Mr. Abelardo de la Espriella, were ordered to promptly remove images that may have reached the cell phones of children across the country, showing a state displaying corpses as trophies. Congressman Santiago Osorio

Th publications were previously rejected by the Ombudsman’s Office, whose director, Iris Marin, urged the government not to “compete with armed groups over who instills the most fear, who humiliates the adversary the most, or who turns death into a display of power.”

In the first video, De la Espriella and Defense Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora walked through rows of body bags, displaying the remains of 23 alleged members of FARC dissident organizations EMC who were killed in the southern Guaviare province.

Among those killed in Operation Azarias were two minor victims of forced recruitment by the guerrillas.

The videos sought to promote the government’s hardline security policy, which vows to kill “narcoterrorists” who refuse to surrender.

World.title: US, Colombia sign memorandums of understanding amid “rebirth” of relations
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hailed the “rebirth” of bilateral relations as they signed memorandums of understanding on nuclear energy and rare earths.

The two leaders met in Barranquilla, where De la Espriella lives, as part of Rubio’s tour through allied countries in the Andean region.

The president and the secretary of state hailed the improvement of ties that were severely disrupted when former President Gustavo Petro was in office.

During a joint press conference, Rubio stressed the need for security in the region, claiming that “the same networks, the same criminal groups that, although they commit their crimes here, they also commit crimes in the U.S., and they damage our people.”

De la Espriella said that as part of the “Barranquilla Agreements,” he asked the US for support for his hardline security policy.

We have proposed to the government—and today I reiterated this proposal to the secretary—the 21st-Century Patriot Plan to modernize aircraft, radars, drones, helicopters, anti-drone systems, air defense, mobility, intelligence, cyber defense, special forces, and maintenance and operations. President Abelardo de la Espriella

The president promised to “start spraying, we are going to target the laboratories, the precursors, the trafficking routes, the drug trafficking kingpins, the armed narco-terrorist organizations—we are going after the money launderers, their criminal assets, and those international networks that pose a grave danger not only to the hemisphere but also to humanity.”

Rubio did not openly commit any US support other than the memorandums of understanding.

The unbinding agreements were part of Rubio’s wish list as the US seeks new sources for rare earths and miners that can be processed outside of China, which the US Government sees as its rival.

With the nuclear energy agenda, Colombia seeks to “strengthen its capacities” with US support. Both governments “reaffirm their commitment to international development and the peaceful use of nuclear energy.”

In order to create policy regarding the memorandums, De la Espriella would need congressional support, which he has yet to seek openly.

World.title: De la Espriella lifts Colombia’s 10-year gun ban
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella lifted a gun ban that had been in place since 2015.

According to De la Espriella, the decision seeks to give “good citizens” a way to defend themselves against “criminals.”

“For years, law-abiding citizens were restricted, while criminals continued to arm themselves to the teeth illegally. That has to change,” said the president on social media platform X.

99.9% of crimes committed with weapons are committed with unlicensed, illegal weapons. Anything said beyond the mathematics is just opinion. Mathematics is an exact science. So I am pleased to sign this decree. President Abelardo de la Espriella

The president said that those who want to carry guns legally must comply with strict regulations and can’t have criminal records.

The ban reactivates previously approved gun licenses and allows citizens older than 25 to purchase approved hand guns from Colombia’s State military industry.

In order to be given a license, a potential gun owner must undergo fitness tests and convince the military authority that his position in society merits a firearm.

The decision has long been awaited by conservative and far-right elements in society, who have claimed that the gun ban made them sitting ducks for extortionists, particularly in the countryside.

Experts consulted by newspaper El Colombiano warned that lifting the gun ban could increase deadly violence, particularly considering Colombia’s violent history and evidence obtained in countries where guns are legal.

“There is no evidence showing that these countries have seen a decrease in theft, extortion, and threats following these measures,” said the director of the Central University’s Security Observatory, Andres Nieto. “On the contrary, the evidence does show an increase in violence among citizens,” the scholar added.

The ban was initially imposed by former President Juan Manuel Santos in 2015 and has since been upheld by his successors.

World.title: Liberal Party joins Colombia’s far-right to form majority coalition
World.content:
The Liberal Party announced that it had joined the congressional coalition of Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

The party, which also supported De la Espriella’s presidential bid, said that it would join the coalition after “extensive deliberation and arduous debate among representatives, senators, and leadership” of Colombia’s oldest political party.

It is worth noting that the discussions between representatives and senators over the past several weeks have revealed disagreements among some members of our caucuses with the current administration, but they also acknowledge President Espriella’s ability to work toward stimulating economic growth, building a talent pool to provide real opportunities for Colombians, and restoring security and respect for institutions. Liberal Party

The liberals’ decision gives the government broad support in Congress and marginalizes the opposition led by the leftist Historic Pact Party.

In the senate, De la Espriella’s right-wing coalition can count on the support of 63 of 103 lawmakers. In the House of Representatives, the coalition consists of 123 of 183 lawmakers.

The Historic Pact, which won the elections and became the biggest party in Congress, was abandoned by the left-liberal Green Alliance party and can count of the support of 28 senators and 44 representatives.

The opposition party has been able to make temporary anti-government alliances with, for example, the far-right Democratic Center party of former President Alvaro Uribe.

World.title: Colombia’s president appoints controversial new spy chief
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella appointed retired army General Jorge Andres Zuluaga as director of the National Intelligence Directorate (DNI) despite pending criminal investigations.

Zuluaga, who spent 30 years with military intelligence, is best known for his participation in Operation Jaque, which liberated former presidential candidate Ingrid Betancourt, three American military contractors and 11 soldiers.

Throughout his career, the 61-year-old former general was deputy commander of the now-defunct Charry Solano intelligence school, commander of the Regional Intelligence #5 and the director of the National Army’s Technical Intelligence Center (CITEC).

Zuluaga received training in the United States and was a diplomatic aide at the Organization of American States.

He was removed as CITEC director in 2014 after prosecution investigators found out that he received intelligence illegally obtained from “Andromeda,” a clandestine intelligence unit that operated from a Bogota internet café.

In October 2024, war crimes tribunal JEP ordered the Prosecutor General’s Office to investigate Zuluaga for his alleged participation in the extermination of the leftist Patriotic Union party when he was the CITEC’s director between 2004 and 2005.

The prosecution has yet to decide whether or not to formally charge the retired general with the crimes he allegedly committed.

Zuluaga, who became a member of the far-right Democratic Center party after he was ejected from the army, has always sustained that he acted within the boundaries of the law.

World.title: Evacuations ordered in Chile as wildfires run amok
World.content:
Chile’s National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response (Senapred) Wednesday ordered the evacuation of 14 communes in the regions of Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía, including Nacimiento, Purén, and Contulmo, which have all been particularly affected by the forest fires.

In messages broadcast through the Emergency Alert System (SAE), the authorities also called on residents to leave their homes to avoid further damage to their health.

It has already been a week since the first wildfires ran amok in south-central Chile despite efforts to contain them. High temperatures, dryness, and strong winds add to the plight of local people and some 5,600 firefighters deployed in the area while helping flocks in from abroad.

”We are entering this part of the week which is the most complex. Today, tomorrow, and the day after we have an alert for high temperatures in several regions of the country that has mobilized a very large effort (…) to prevent the fires from spreading,“ Interior Minister Carolina Tohá said regarding the 311 active fires, of which 89 are being fought. The Senapred also said 180 fires were under control, and 309,747 hectares have been affected.

”If the temperature rises and the wind increases we can indeed have more problems, and we already have many fires,” Spanish Lieutenant Colonel Carlos Javier Martín Traverso told AFP. Traverso’s Air Operations Section of the Military Emergency Unit (UME) arrived in Chile on Sunday to join the firefighting efforts.

Over 309,000 hectares have been consumed in the regions of Maule, Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía with the death toll standing at 24, plus 2,180 people injured as 1,180 houses were destroyed, leaving 5,560 people homeless.

There seems to be a seamless scientific consensus that fires are the result of human actions, either by intentionality or carelessness, although the drought that has hit Chile for 13 years adds to the aggressiveness of the fires.

In this scenario, President Gabriel Boric Font has announced a curfew in the areas of Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía where a state of catastrophe is in force, in order to guarantee the security and tranquility of

the families affected by the crisis. Defense authorities working on the sites will determine the restriction’s schedule.

“We have 24 people dead nationwide, three are from Santa Juana and we do not want there to be even one more,” Boric told reporters after visiting the area.

The number of fatalities was updated to 24 after two bodies were determined to belong to people who had died before the fires broke out.

Meanwhile, Biobío Governor Rodrigo Díaz said he was certain about “people criminally setting fires.”

“I have reports from police, firefighters, of people who have been setting fires. I do not have indications, but certainties, we need more patrols,” he insisted in a radio interview.

“We have fire outbreaks at the southern exit of Contulmo, different places where fires were set 300 meters away from each other, I could see it, nobody told me about it. The mayor of Mulchén told me how fires were lit in the four cardinal points, I have reports from the police, the Fire Department, from people who have been setting fires. I do not have indications, but certainties, we need more patrols in the area,” he explained.

President Boric’s Regional Delegate Daniela Dresdner said eight people had been arrested for “irresponsible and suspicious attitudes with respect to the setting of fires. This was due to citizen complaints and patrols by the Navy.”

“We are asking that all these conducts be denounced and we are filing a lawsuit for all these denunciations to [be] prosecute[d],” she added.

The Biobío Regional Prosecutor’s Office called on the citizenry to e-mail all data regarding criminal behavior to fiscaliaincendios@gmail.com, including pictures, videos, audios, or written information as to the probable causes of the fires, which will be handled confidentially. (Merco Press)

World.title: Chile’s wildfires death toll reaches 24
World.content:
Chilean authorities spoke Sunday of 24 fatalities, nearly 1,000 people injured, and some 800 houses destroyed in the past five days by wildfires spreading fast in amid a highly-irregular heat wave with strong winds and temperatures above 40°C in areas 500 km south of Santiago.

The death toll reached 24 after the death of one of the injured people who had been hospitalized in Angol, Undersecretary of the Interior Manuel Monsalve explained. “The risk situation in the country remains” in the regions of Ñuble, Biobío, and La Araucanía, and in certain localities of the central region of Maule, he said. A red alert was also decreed Sunday in communes of the southern regions of Los Ríos and Los Lagos due to the appearance of new fire outbreaks. He also pointed out that 26 of the 997 people injured were in serious condition.

“I came home from work and I was already without anything, without a house. I was left on the street, with my arms crossed, now with my son, and my wife, in a tent. I have no fodder for my animals,” a resident of the town of Purén, in the Araucanía region, told Televisión Nacional de Chile (TVN).

Meanwhile, President Gabriel Boric Font attended the wake of a firefighter in the town of Coronel. ”Chile is crying with you. I am here to tell you that you are not alone, that the family of Yesenia (Muñoz, the deceased firefighter) will not be alone,” he said.

According to Chile’s National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response (Senapred), the number of fires being fought went down from 87 to 51. “We are experiencing a small window of improving weather conditions during Sunday and Monday. That means that we are not with extremely high temperatures,” Monsalve said.

Undersecretary Monsalve also told reporters that 10 people have been arrested for their responsibility in starting some of the fires for which the red alert was still maintained. Of the total number of fires, 22 occurred Sunday for a total of 283 active fires, of which 151 were under control and 71 are being fought.

Given the magnitude of the fires in size and number, international help has been summoned. “We have just sent a plane to Chile with a contingent of the Military Emergency Unit to collaborate in extinguishing and controlling the fires that are raging in the country. All our support to the Chilean people,” tweeted Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Chile’s Foreign Ministry also said assistance was being coordinated with Argentina, Brazil, Ecuador, the United States, and Mexico, while Boric’s administration has declared a constitutional state of catastrophe in the regions of Ñuble, Biobío and La Araucanía, to speed up additional resources while restricting free transit and involving military forces to contain the disaster.

In 2017, another chain of fires destroyed some 460,000 hectares, left 11 people dead, nearly 6,000 injured, and more than 1,500 homes burned.

Monsalve also warned that this week high temperatures will continue, as well as the risk of low humidity and strong gusts of wind, which will make it difficult to extinguish the flames. – MercoPress

World.title: Parts of Chile under red alert for major forest fires in central region
World.content:
The Government of Chile has declared a “red alert” in the central part of the country due to the heat wave stemming from 39 major forest fires as the wave keeps spreading throughout the country, most of them in Araucania (17) but also in Bío Bío (7), Ñuble (7), Maule (4), Los Lagos (3), and one in the Santiago Metropolitan Region.

The National Service for Disaster Prevention and Response reported that in addition to the 39 fires currently being fought, there were four others under observation, while 141 were already under control, and 20 had already been extinguished.

Authorities ordered a series of preventive evacuations in several towns, as well as the interruption of highway traffic in the most affected areas where 181 hectares of scrubland and pastureland were burned out, threatening nearby homes.

The main cause for the fires is said to be the summer high temperatures which reached 41 degrees Celsius in the Chillán area.

Meteorologists forecast that the heat wave will last until Sunday. The last major fires to affect Chile were recorded in the summer of 2017 when the flames swept through entire villages, causing 11 deaths and more than 580 thousand hectares affected.

The state-owned National Forestry Corporation (Conaf) reported that in the Ñuble region, the fire has already affected some 550 hectares in the area of Chillán Viejo and another 200 hectares in another town near the regional capital, burning infrastructure and some houses.

Agriculture Minister Esteban Valenzuela told reporters that in addition to the heat wave, the dry and hot Puelche wind from the eastern cordillera was also expected in the central-southern zone. Valenzuela also announced the temporary closure of seven national parks from Santiago to the south in the Metropolitan, Ñuble, Biobío, La Araucanía, and Aysén regions to prevent new fires, and also ordered the evacuation of rural areas of Ñuble, where simultaneous forest fires were reported.

– MercoPress

World.title: Chilean airlines will reimburse cost of boarding taxes under certain conditions
World.content:
Chile’s national Consumer Service, Sernac is calling all consumers who purchased tickets directly from airlines between 2015 and 201l and did not make use of them, to claim from the companies the reimbursement of the boarding taxes paid.

Following on a Voluntary Collective Procedure reached at the beginning of 2020 with LATAM, and at the end of 2021 with Sky, Avianca, Jetsmart, Aerolineas Argentinas and COPA, the airlines agreed to reimburse the boarding taxes cost for flights not done between May first 2015 and 24 December 2021, with the exception of Jetsmart, which only started operations in Chile in July 2017.

Accordingly the universe of beneficiaries reached 1.108.416 passengers and involved some US$ 12 million for domestic flights and US$ 1,4 million for international flights. The amount to be reimbursed to each potential passenger depends on the distance to travel and if it was domestic of international travel.

In Chile the domestic boarding tax is equivalent to some US$ 14 and overseas US$ 50. Allegedly following the agreement the companies were to inform the beneficiaries of their reimbursements.

Reimbursements can also be checked by filling forms at the airlines’ offices. For further information on the agreement and the sums involved consumers are invited to check the web.

World.title: Remembering Steve Anderson
World.content:
BENJAMIN WITTE

I was neither the first nor the last of the many interns and editors who peopled the office of the Santiago Times during the quarter century founder Steve Anderson captained the ship. But for whatever reason, I stuck around longer than most, and it was with great sadness that I learned yesterday about the automobile accident that ended his life.

My first encounter with Steve came in late 2002, after he had offered me the editor’s job—sight unseen, via e-mail—and I accepted, knowing only that I’d earn about US$500 a month and should show up in Santiago with an AP style guide and a copy of Strunk and White’s The Elements of Style. That it all seemed a bit rushed and loosey-goosey gave me pause for concern, but I was eager for an excuse to return to Chile, so hopped on a plane and flew down from Costa Rica.

Still, after our first meeting, I wondered just how wise my decision really was. It was then that I realized the Santiago Times wasn’t, as I’d imagined, a print paper. It was Internet-based, with a rudimentary website that was only half functioning. “We got hacked,” Steve told me. He also explained that he was living at that moment in Puerto Montt—1,000 kilometers to the south—and that he was recovering still from a recent and quite serious car accident. It had been a very bad year, he said.

I gave the gig a chance, though, and things gradually improved. Some energetic new interns trickled in, as they always did at the Santiago Times. A talented British/Australian writer showed up too, and I asked Steve to hire him as a kind of co-editor. The business couldn’t really afford another paid staff member, but Steve honored my request, and for the next year or so we had a great run. Then the money ran out.

“I can’t afford to pay you both, so one of you has to go,” Steve told us one morning. “I’ll leave it up to you two to decide which one.” And so we did—over a liter of beer, even though it was like nine-something in the morning. The co-editor (still a dear friend of mine) offered to go. But I’d leave too, I decided. A month or so later. The job had run its course, I thought.

We were frustrated and certainly taken aback—especially by the “decide amongst yourselves who stays and goes” part of the equation. And yet, neither of us was really surprised, because even then, we’d seen enough of Steve and his herky-jerky management style to know that this was precisely the kind of situation that could and would, as it turned out, unfold.

We couldn’t really be angry either. Or at least not stay angry. Because again, with Steve, what you saw is what you got. He was passionate about his project, but not always clear about how to make it grow. Often he’d have a new idea, and then charge ahead. And in those cases, there’d be a flurry of positive changes—new computers maybe, a new paid staff person, a larger office space. But then a particularly capable group of interns would move on, money would run scarce, the whole operation would contract, and we’d be back to square one, or so it felt.

I know this because later I joined Steve for a second, longer stint. What never varied, though, was his fighting spirit. A feisty advocate for the underdog, he was always chomping to champion a good cause—demanding accountability for human rights violations, defending the environment, shining a light on corruption and hypocrisy.

The Santiago Times was his platform, and he committed himself tooth-and-nail to making it survive, if not prosper. And in the meantime, the interns, editors, photographers and other collaborators kept coming through. They kept using Steve’s office and humble little publication as a landing point for early-career, working-abroad experiences, and as a launching pad for further adventures and professional endeavors.

If there was a method to Steve’s madcap approach, it was that with each new idea he had for the Santiago Times, with each new push to improve or revive it, he bought the business a little more time. Months turned into years and then decades. And all the while, people like myself were given an opportunity to work and learn—in large part through trial and error, because although Steve had things to teach, he also gave us space to teach ourselves.

It was his special tenacity, though, that kept the whole thing going, that gave so many people the chance, year after year, to develop their skills. We had fun too. So much fun. The office on Av. Santa María produced lasting, globe-spanning friendships, even love stories. And that was also part of Steve’s gift to us all.

He was an unabashed eccentric. Smart. Complicated. He had an entrepreneurial spirit but no real nose for business. Steve was a lawyer who wrote about politics and fruit exports. An editor with a penchant for typos. Part idealist, part cynic. A campaigner with no patience for diplomacy. He was perpetually cash-strapped, but generous. He was impulsive and impatient at times, but also deeply committed—to his various projects and causes, and to his family and colleagues. He was a teacher and a mentor. A doting father. A friend.

Goodbye Steve. Paz. And thank you.

World.title: Anti-vaccine mandate protests spread across the country, crippling Canada-U.S. trade
World.content:
Speaking to reporters at a press conference in Ottawa, Emergency Preparedness Minister Bill Blair said the blockade at Windsor’s Ambassador Bridge is particularly alarming because a quarter of all Canada-U.S. trade moves through that one crossing, which connects Canada with Detroit and points beyond.

Hundreds of millions of dollars worth of products have been held back for three days as 50 to 75 vehicles and about 100 anti-mandate protesters camp out on the main road that leads on and off the bridge.

The Canada Border Service Agency (CBSA) has closed the bridge to commercial traffic temporarily, diverting trucks to the Blue Water Bridge in Sarnia, Ont. instead. CBSA is reporting wait times in excess of four hours to make the short trip across to Port Huron, Mich.

We’ve seen the criminal acts, acts of thuggery and the obnoxiousness that they’ve inflicted on the people of Ottawa. Now they’re blocking the highways leading into our ports of entry. They’re putting their foot on the throats of all Canadians.

Labour unions representing auto workers have reported some idled Windsor plants have sent workers home while the trucker convoy holds up much-needed parts coming from the U.S.

Transport Minister Omar Alghabra said central Canada could soon see empty store shelves because so much of the region’s fresh food and produce comes into the country across that bridge.

To be honest, I find it ironic that the same people who were trying to sell Canadians fake stories about empty shelves are now causing those shelves to go empty, Alghabra said.

Windsor Mayor Drew Dilkens said the protesters appear to be determined to stay. They feel such a passion for this particular cause that they’re willing to die for it, he said.

Speaking briefly to reporters before question period, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said his government is working with Ontario and the City of Windsor to put an end to the blockade.

World.title: Excellent prospects for Mercosur beef exports, except Argentina
World.content:
